About 1st Formations
At 1st Formations, we empower entrepreneurs to start, run, and grow their businesses with confidence.
Running a business shouldn’t be slowed down by company formation, statutory compliance, accounting, or payroll. From day one, these essentials should be seamless, reliable, and intelligently handled — freeing founders to focus on building and scaling.
We’re a leading UK provider of company formation and compliance services, building a modern, fully integrated technology platform that supports founders at every stage of their journey. Our platform brings together formation, compliance, accounting, payroll, and ongoing business support in one cohesive experience.
No stitched-together services. No legacy workflows disguised as software.
Just a single, scalable platform built for ambitious founders who want to move fast, stay compliant, and grow with confidence.
Why Join Us Now?
You’ll be joining a business with strong momentum, clear direction, and real opportunity for progression.
£18m annual revenue, including £9m ARR
Over 1 million companies formed
Certified B Corp and Carbon Neutral Business
Forecast to grow 5x–10x over the next three years
The Role
As Product Owner (Data & Delivery), you'll own one product area end to end, from requirement through to released, accepted and measured. Working to the Senior Product Manager, you'll turn agreed outcomes into well-shaped requirements, a prioritised backlog and released changes that work for customers, operations and commercial teams.
The role is data-led. You'll define the measures that matter for your area, query the data yourself rather than waiting to be told what it shows, and work with our Data and Analytics Lead to turn data needs into clear specifications. Quality is part of the job too: you'll own business acceptance, defect triage and release readiness, with changes you specified accepted by our Product Quality Analyst, and theirs by you. You'll also play a significant part in our platform migration programme, covering requirements, scoping, prototyping and testing.
Key Responsibilities
Own delivery of your product workstreams end to end, from refined requirement to release and post-release review.
Turn outcomes set by the Senior Product Manager or CPO into clear epics, user stories and acceptance criteria.
Own and prioritise the backlog, running refinement, planning and review with engineering and design.
Manage dependencies and risks, and keep operations, support and commercial teams informed on scope and timing.
Define success measures, baselines and targets for each workstream before build starts.
Query data directly to size problems, test assumptions and challenge analytical outputs before they're relied on.
Analyse funnels, cohorts and drop-off to find where journeys fail and where the commercial opportunity sits.
Design and interpret A/B tests, and specify tracking for every change so it's measurable from release.
Own reporting for your area, recommending whether to iterate, scale or stop after release.
Shape and test platform migration work, including requirements, data mapping, prototyping, reconciliation and dry runs.
Own business acceptance, defect triage and release readiness, accepting the Product Quality Analyst's changes and having yours accepted by them.
Validate end-to-end customer journeys, including compliance-sensitive steps, and make sure each release has the documentation the business needs.
What We Are Looking For
5+ years' experience as a Product Owner, Product Analyst or in Product Operations within a digital product environment, including time owning delivery of a workstream rather than supporting one.
Strong hands-on data skills, including writing your own SQL and working confidently with large datasets, so you can answer your own questions and form a view from the data.
Sound analytical judgement: you separate signal from noise, recognise when a number isn't reliable, and say so.
Experience using funnel, cohort and retention analysis to change what a team builds.
Experience designing and interpreting A/B tests, including sample sizing and an honest reading of inconclusive results.
Experience defining tracking and event requirements, using tools such as Mixpanel, Amplitude or GA4.
Confidence writing clear, testable user stories and acceptance criteria, and running refinement with engineering in an Agile team using tools such as Linear, Jira or Asana.
Experience of business or user acceptance testing (BAT/UAT), validating end-to-end customer journeys across web platforms, and holding the line on readiness before release.
The ability to take a defined outcome and run it to delivery, making sound trade-offs between value, effort, risk and dependency.
Commercial awareness of how product changes affect conversion, revenue, cost to serve and operational load.
Clear written and verbal communication across Product, Engineering, Data, Operations, Support and Commercial teams, with the pace and pragmatism to know when good enough is the right answer.
A degree in a numerate, business or technology discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Data or platform migration experience (requirements, data mapping, reconciliation and testing) is a strong advantage, and experience in a regulated environment.
What We Offer
£65-75k and comprehensive benefits package
Hybrid working model
Real opportunities for progression as the business scales
The chance to influence both customer experience and product development
A culture that values ownership, impact, and continuous learning

We consider all applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, criminal history, disability, or gender identity. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

# Project Manager – Change, Efficiency & Process Improvement
**Salary:** £45,000 per year (pro rata)
**Hours:** 25 hours a week
**Location:** Hybrid with travel to ABL offices as required
**Closing Date:** 18th October 2026
**Quote reference:** **ABL 928**
**Role Purpose:**
ABL is seeking a highly motivated and self-sufficient Project Manager to lead and deliver a portfolio of business change, operational efficiency, and process improvement initiatives across the organisation. The role will be responsible for managing multiple concurrent projects from inception through to implementation and benefits realisation, ensuring delivery against agreed scope, timescales, budgets and quality standards.
The successful candidate will possess a strong understanding of project management methodologies, particularly PRINCE2, alongside excellent stakeholder engagement, planning and organisational skills. They must be comfortable working independently with minimal supervision whilst operating effectively across multiple workstreams and business functions.
**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**
The successful candidate will manage a portfolio of change, transformation, efficiency and process improvement projects, leading them through the full project lifecycle from business case development and initiation through to implementation and closure. You will develop and maintain project plans, monitor progress, manage risks and dependencies, and ensure projects deliver their agreed objectives and measurable business benefits. Working closely with departments across the organisation, you will identify opportunities to improve efficiency, streamline processes and reduce costs, facilitate process mapping and improvement workshops, and support the implementation of sustainable new ways of working. You will apply PRINCE2 principles to ensure effective project governance, maintain project documentation and RAID logs, and provide clear reporting to senior management and the Change Board. The role will involve building strong stakeholder relationships, facilitating meetings and decision-making forums, and influencing stakeholders to support successful outcomes. You will also define and monitor benefits, ensure improvements are embedded into business operations, and contribute to continuous improvement and lessons learned activities, working alongside the Health Equity Performance Lead where operational or process change is required.
**Key Success Measures**
**The successful candidate will:**
• Deliver projects on time, within scope and to agreed quality standards.
• Successfully manage a portfolio of multiple concurrent projects.
• Achieve measurable operational efficiencies and business improvements.
• Maintain accurate, timely and effective project governance and reporting.
• Demonstrate strong stakeholder satisfaction and engagement.
• Ensure project benefits are realised and sustained following implementation.
This role offers an excellent opportunity for an experienced Project Manager to play a key role in delivering ABL’s strategic change agenda and driving tangible operational improvements across the organisation.

International Regulatory Strategy
* Own and evolve the company's ex-US regulatory strategy, prioritizing EU IVDR (technical documentation, Notified Body engagement, serve as PRRC, EU Declaration of Conformity) and Health Canada (Medical Device License applications, License amendments, Class III/IV IVD requirements) as the initial core markets.
* Build the regulatory roadmap for future international expansion (e.g., UKCA, TGA, NMPA, other APAC/LATAM markets), including market-entry sequencing, gap assessments, and localization requirements.

## From the employer
WHO WE ARE
Enterprise work still moves by hand: copy-pasting between spreadsheets, endless email threads, and clunky legacy UIs. We started Duvo to end that for good.
We've already earned the trust of a range of customers, and our agents are helping them automate business-critical processes. We are growing fast, but to win from here we need exceptional people; that's where you come in.
WHAT WE ARE BUILDING
We're building the AI operations platform for large enterprises, currently focused on retail and consumer packaged goods customers. In Duvo, customers build AI agents that execute work wherever it needs to get done—SAP, spreadsheets, supplier portals, email, APIs, you name it. Duvo is heavy on browser and computer use.
In Duvo, business users specify the outcome; agents plan, act, request approvals on exceptions, and learn with every run. To help customers understand what to automate, we also help them map their processes by digesting interviews and internal documentation, which gets our foot in the door. We start with automating the parts of companies that we know best (category management, supply chain, finance ops) where we can show value fast, then expand to adjacent functions and sectors.
Velocity is our moat: ship fast, iterate faster, compound learning.
THE ROLE
You will own the AI infrastructure that makes our agents reliable, fast, and safe in production. You build the agent runtime, evaluation pipelines, context management systems, tool orchestration, and the observability tooling that lets agents execute end-to-end work for enterprise customers.
This is applied AI systems engineering, not ML research. You ship production systems that use LLMs, retrieval, and agent orchestration—and you're accountable for their reliability, cost, and quality in the real world.
Your unit of ownership: the AI platform layer — agent runtime, context management, tool execution, evaluation harnesses, and prompt engineering for system behaviors. You own sandbox behavior and agent runtime logic; SRE owns sandbox infrastructure and capacity.
We're a growing product team scaling into multiple initiatives, each with a lead, engineers, a design engineer, and an AI-focused engineer.
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
These are non-negotiables—the things we'll specifically evaluate you on:
- Experience building production AI systems. Not research — making LLMs reliable at scale. You've dealt with prompt engineering, context management, tool use, or agent orchestration in production.
- Shipping and ownership. You've taken ambiguous AI problems to production with measurable outcomes. You own the full lifecycle — build, evaluate, deploy, monitor, iterate.
- System design for AI. You can design systems that handle the unique challenges of AI: non-deterministic outputs, context window limits, tool execution failures, and cost optimization. You think about reliability, cost, and latency as first-class concerns.
- Evaluation design. You can build evaluation frameworks that catch regressions, measure quality, and give the team confidence to ship AI features. You understand failure taxonomies and know how to create meaningful test sets.
- Debugging and diagnosis. You're hypothesis-driven when things break. You can trace failures across model behavior, data pipelines, and infrastructure to find root causes.
- Judgment as AI evolves. You'll make build-vs-integrate decisions on AI infrastructure with incomplete benchmarks, and course-correct fast as models and providers evolve.
YOU MIGHT ALSO
- Have scalable, distributed-system instincts—you've designed and operated systems that handle high throughput and complex failure modes.
- Have a strong sense for security in AI systems—prompt injection, insecure output handling, supply chain risks.
- Have contributed to open-source AI tooling or infrastructure projects.
THIS IS NOT FOR YOU IF
- You want an ML research role — we don't train models.
- You primarily want to build user-facing product features and UI.
LOCATION
We're looking for people within two hours of Prague (CET), so the team overlaps for most of the working day.
OUR TECH STACK
- GCP (Cloud Run, GKE, GCS)
- Terraform, Docker
- Datadog
- TypeScript and Python services (you'll read and occasionally modify application code, but deep language expertise isn't required)
- Postgres, Redis
HOW WE WORK
These are real tradeoffs we've made, not aspirations:
- Initiative-driven. We organize around customer problems, not org charts. Problems surface through product feedback, competitive analysis, and direct customer conversations — then we prioritize, build, and ship weekly.
- Customer-obsessed. We solve real problems, not hypothetical ones. Features that don't move customer metrics get cut.
- Iterative by default. We ship small, learn fast, and never get attached to yesterday's code. This means things break sometimes — we fix forward.
- AI-first leverage. We use AI to move faster and focus human time where it matters most. If a tool can do it, a person shouldn't.
- Direct feedback. We give each other actionable feedback immediately. This can feel uncomfortable — we think that's worth it.
- Autonomy with accountability. We trust people to make decisions and hold them to outcomes, not process.

- A real AI product with real customers. You're not building demos or internal tools. Enterprise customers use what you ship, and their feedback drives what you build next.
- A sharp, motivated team that values ownership and candor.
HOW WE HIRE
We respect your time and aim to move fast:

2. Technical interview (online, ~1 hour). Meet the team. We'll go deeper on your experience, system design, product thinking, and collaboration. No trick questions — we want to see how you think and build.

# **Job Details:**
### ## **Job Description:**
Altera is seeking a talented Senior FPGA IP Solutions Engineer to join the Robotics Technology Group in Marlow, UK. This hands-on role focuses on the design, verification, and delivery of high-performance FPGA IP and solutions that enable next-generation robotics and industrial automation systems.
Working within a small, highly technical team, you will develop reusable RTL IP for sensor ingestion, data pre-processing, fusion pipelines, and real-time compute accelerators for robotics use cases. Your primary ownership is the RTL IP and the low-level software interface (HAL / driver API) that exposes it—covering micro-architecture, RTL implementation, simulation, timing closure, and Quartus Prime / Platform Designer integration. You will also maintain a clear awareness of how that IP fits into the broader system and solution stack, collaborating with software and systems engineers on reference designs and customer-facing robotics platforms.
This role emphasizes deep FPGA IP and HAL craftsmanship—high-performance RTL, verification and simulation, and clean low-level APIs—while requiring enough system-level awareness to integrate cleanly into end-to-end robotics solutions.
**Key Responsibilities**
**FPGA IP Design & Architecture**
* Design, implement, and optimize high-performance soft IP in Verilog/SystemVerilog for robotics and industrial solutions
* Define and maintain low-level HAL / driver APIs that expose IP capabilities to embedded and host software
* Develop RTL for sensor ingestion, pre-processing, fusion, and mathematical / DSP algorithms mapped efficiently to FPGA fabric
* Apply strong FPGA architecture awareness to drive resource allocation (ALMs, DSP, memory), Fmax, and power/performance trade-offs
* Integrate IP into system designs using Quartus Prime and Platform Designer (Avalon / AXI interconnects, streaming and memory-mapped fabrics), with awareness of full-stack solution integration
**Verification, Simulation & Timing Closure**
* Write and maintain testbenches; perform functional simulation and regression of IP and subsystems
* Drive static timing analysis (STA), timing closure, clock-domain crossing (CDC) correctness, and constraint quality
* Debug designs through simulation, SignalTap / on-chip debug, and lab bring-up as required
* Contribute to design examples, simulation models, and technical documentation for internal and customer use
**Design Infrastructure & Delivery**
* Work effectively within engineering infrastructure including Perforce, GitHub, Jenkins, and TeamCity
* Support continuous integration, regression flows, and release quality for IP and reference designs
* Collaborate with software, systems, and applications engineers on HW/SW co-design and platform integration, including robotics software stacks where applicable (e.g. ROS2)
* Support platform bring-up, validation, and resolution of customer or internal technical issues
### ## **Qualifications:**
**Minimum Qualifications**
* Min 10 + Years experience with BSc / MSc (or equivalent) in Electrical/Electronic Engineering (EEE), Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline
* Strong production experience in RTL design (Verilog and/or SystemVerilog) targeting FPGAs
* Hands-on experience with RTL verification and simulation (e.g. ModelSim/Questa, VCS, or equivalent)
* Proven ability to close timing and optimize resource utilization on real FPGA designs
* Working knowledge of Quartus Prime and Platform Designer (or equivalent FPGA toolchain and system integration flows)
* Experience debugging FPGA designs using on-chip instrumentation (e.g. SignalTap Logic Analyzer) and hands-on bring-up and debug on development kits and physical boards
* Familiarity with modern engineering infrastructure such as Perforce and/or GitHub, and CI systems such as Jenkins and/or TeamCity
* Strong analytical, debug, and problem-solving skills, with clear written and verbal communication
**Preferred Qualifications**
* Experience developing high-performance, reusable FPGA soft IP (streaming pipelines, DSP, interconnect, or compute accelerators)
* Deep understanding of FPGA architecture, pipelining, CDC, constraints, and STA best practices
* Experience with sensor data ingestion, pre-processing, sensor fusion, and/or mapping mathematical algorithms into hardware
* Prior exposure to robotics systems and robotics software stacks (e.g. ROS / ROS2) is a strong plus, enabling closer alignment of FPGA IP capabilities with end-application requirements
* Experience with motor control topics (e.g. FOC, PWM generation, encoders/resolvers, current/torque loops, or real-time motion control on FPGA) is a plus
* Scripting experience (Tcl, Python, and/or Perl) for automation of build, simulation, and timing flows
* Familiarity with Avalon and/or AXI protocols, low-level HAL / driver APIs, and HW/SW integration with embedded processors or accelerators

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
**About Beneficial Deployments**
Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences - focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.
**About the Role**
We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. This is a partner-facing role: you'll support nonprofits, research institutes, academic medical centres and public-sector funders as they use Claude to get treatments to patients with rare and neglected diseases, where there is little or no commercial incentive to fund development.
The role focuses on two areas where we think Claude can help these partners today. The first is clinical trials. Trials in these diseases have small patient populations, investigator-led or nonprofit funding and little operational support, and they often stall on protocol quality, operational risk and site start-up. Claude can help teams design better trials and start them sooner. The second is drug repurposing: finding new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.
You'll advise and embed in partners' teams, building alongside their engineers, scientists and clinicians.
**Responsibilities**
* Work with partners' trial teams to design, review and prioritise clinical trials with Claude: drafting and reviewing protocols and statistical analysis plans, and flagging enrolment and operational risks.
* Build and validate tools that help partners find new uses for approved, mostly off-patent medicines in rare and neglected diseases, from literature, omics and patient data, and assemble the evidence so the partner can decide the next step.
* Build reusable infrastructure other institutions can adopt (MCP servers for biomedical data sources, agent skills, benchmarks grounded in real clinical questions), and feed what you learn in the field back to product, engineering and research.
**You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have**

## Job Description
**Role Overview**
The Change Manager is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing organizational change management activities to support successful delivery of strategic initiatives. The role ensures that impacted stakeholders are engaged, prepared, and supported throughout the transformation lifecycle. Working closely with the Corporate PMO, business sponsors, HR, Communications, and project teams, the Change Manager develops change strategies, communication plans, and training approaches that help embed new ways of working across the company.
The Change Manager ensures that transformation initiatives are adopted effectively and that business impacts are minimized during delivery. This position operates under the direction of the Head of Corporate PMO and contributes to the company’s overall strategic execution capability.
**Key Responsibilities**
**Change Planning & Strategy**
* Develops change management strategies and plans for initiatives led or supported by the PMO.
* Identifies impacted stakeholders, target audiences, change readiness, and adoption risks.
* Defines change scope, objectives, and success criteria in alignment with sponsors and PMO standards.
* Stakeholder Engagement & Communication
* Prepares stakeholder engagement plans and ensures transparent communication across the organization.
* Coordinates with HR and Communications to deliver messages, updates, and awareness campaigns.
* Facilitates workshops, briefings, and sessions to drive understanding and alignment.
**Training & Capability Support**
* Identifies training needs and develops training content in collaboration with business owners.
* Supports execution of training plans, materials, and enablement activities.
* Ensures end users have the knowledge and tools required to adopt new processes or systems.
* Change Impact & Readiness Assessment
* Conducts readiness assessments, impact analyses, and risk evaluations.
* Helps project teams understand business impacts and necessary mitigations.
* Tracks change readiness throughout the project lifecycle.
* Adoption & Benefits Enablement
* Monitors adoption metrics, end-user feedback, and change effectiveness.
* Identifies areas requiring additional reinforcement or communication.
* Supports activities that contribute to achieving intended benefits and sustainable adoption.
**Governance & PMO Collaboration**
* Ensures all change management activities follow PMO methodologies and templates.
* Provides change progress reporting as part of project governance cycles.
* Contributes to lessons learned and continuous improvement of management practices.

* 3–5 years of experience in organizational change management or transformation roles.
* Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence without authority.
* Experience conducting impact assessments, readiness evaluations, and adoption tracking.
* Ability to design and deliver communication and training plans.
* High level of organization and ability to work effectively across business units.

## Job Description
**LEEDS BASED**
**Prudential Policy Directorate**
The Prudential Policy Directorate (PPD) is responsible for designing, negotiating internationally and implementing effective prudential regulation in order to remove or reduce systemic risks, promote the safety and soundness of PRA-regulated firms and ensure appropriate protection for insurance policyholders. PPD supports both the Prudential Regulation Committee and Financial Policy Committee in fulfilling their objectives.
**The Prudential Framework Division**
The Prudential Framework Division promotes financial stability and resilience in a changing world by working with others to deliver world-class banking prudential policy and thought leadership.
We do this by shaping, maintaining the integrity of, and explaining the capital frameworks, macroprudential toolkit, liquidity policy, FSCS protection and regulatory perimeter, including considering innovation.
The Division plays an active role in policy development, implementation, evaluation, and horizon scanning. It works closely with colleagues across the Bank and with external stakeholders. Analysis and research are undertaken across the Division to ensure that the Bank remains at the forefront of the intellectual debate on prudential policy.
**Liquidity Policy Team**
This role will sit in the Liquidity Policy Team. The team is recognised internationally for its thought leadership in prudential liquidity regulation and places a high value on rigorous analysis, intellectual curiosity and evidence-based policy. Its work has a direct impact on firms, markets and financial stability in the UK and internationally.
The team works closely with colleagues across the Bank, including Supervision, SRS, Markets, and Legal. As key prudential standards are developed internationally, the team also engages directly with overseas authorities and international bodies, including the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
**Job Description**
This is a permanent opportunity for a Lead Policy Analyst at Scale F within the Liquidity Policy Team. The roleholder will play a key role in the design and delivery of liquidity policy at the Bank of England, leading policy development across a range of high-profile issues and contributing directly to externally visible policy outputs and senior-level decision-making.
The role offers the opportunity to shape prudential liquidity policy, develop technical expertise and contribute to domestic and international policy discussions. The successful candidate will work closely with colleagues across the Bank and with external stakeholders to develop evidence-based policy solutions to complex prudential issues.
Near-term priorities for the team include finalising the PRA’s policy statement following the feedback on the consultation paper on modernising the liquidity framework in the wake of the March 2023 banking turmoil. Looking forward the team is developing analysis and policy proposals relating to the accounting treatment of liquid assets, including with unrealised losses attached and their interaction with the liquidity and wider prudential frameworks. Also contributing to implementation of relevant international standards, including the Basel standard for the prudential treatment of cryptoassets. The role will also involve contributing to international policy discussions, including Basel liquidity policy work.
**Role Responsibilities**
The role will include:
* Leading policy development across a range of liquidity policy issues, producing analysis and recommendations to support senior decision-making, policy implementation and external policy outputs.
* Drafting policy papers, consultation and publication material, briefing notes and submissions, and communicating complex issues clearly to specialist, non-specialist and senior audiences.
* Leading engagement with internal and external stakeholders, building effective relationships, navigating differing perspectives and influencing policy outcomes.
* Contributing to the development, implementation and evaluation of liquidity policy, including analysing complex issues, assessing policy options and supporting the delivery of policy outcomes.
* Using quantitative analysis alongside policy judgement and qualitative evidence to inform policy development, including working with regulatory and other relevant data, assessing the quality and limitations of evidence, developing and challenging analytical approaches, and translating findings into practical policy conclusions.
* Managing multiple workstreams, balancing competing priorities and delivering high-quality outputs to demanding deadlines while working collaboratively across organisational boundaries.
* Contributing to the continued development of the team's technical and analytical capability.
**Role Requirements**
Minimum Criteria
* Analytical capability, including experience of analysing complex policy, regulatory or financial-sector issues, applying quantitative and qualitative analysis, and developing evidence-based recommendations.
* Ability to work effectively with colleagues from different disciplines and backgrounds to solve problems and deliver outcomes.
* Ability to communicate complex issues clearly and concisely, both in writing and verbally.
Essential Criteria
* Ability to use and interpret data and other information, draw clear conclusions, and present findings in a clear and accessible way to support policy development and decision-making.
* Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, including the ability to build consensus, navigate differing perspectives, and engage effectively with senior stakeholders.
* Experience of developing, implementing or advising on policy, regulatory, supervisory, markets, risk or related initiatives.
* Demonstrable ability to prioritise effectively, manage competing demands and deliver high-quality outputs to demanding deadlines.
* Ability to develop technical expertise and apply it to influence policy development, decision-making or broader organisational thinking, particularly in complex or uncertain situations.
* Ability to understand how individual policy issues contribute to wider prudential, financial stability and organisational objectives.
Desirable Criteria
* Knowledge of prudential regulation, financial stability issues, banking business models, or prudential supervision.
* Experience of international policy development or engagement with international standards.
* Experience of working on issues involving significant uncertainty or evolving regulatory frameworks.
* Good understanding of liquidity, capital, markets, payments, or other prudential risk frameworks.
**This job advert will be assessed alongside the IRP Scale F job advert. Applicants should indicate whether they wish to be considered for one or both opportunities in the ‘skills and experience’ question.**
**Our Approach to Inclusion**
The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve.
At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public.
We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed.
From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team.
Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application.
**Salary and Benefits Information**
We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate.
Salary circa £50,320 - £56,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below:
* Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time.
* A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool.
* An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits.
* 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits.
* Private medical insurance and income protection.
**National Security Vetting Process**
Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice.
The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis.
**The Application Process**
**Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully.** All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process.

job_title: Senior Data Engineer – Data Products & AI
job_description:
**About Beacon Intelligence**
Beacon Intelligence delivers data and insights that help R&D scientists develop better pharmaceuticals, faster than ever before.
Our focus is simple: we curate high-accuracy data enriched and transformed with AI. This is delivered through a range of platforms, increasingly via AI-native products and features that enable customers to extract insights faster than ever before.
This is a rare opportunity to make a meaningful impact on patients’ lives worldwide.
---
**The Role**
As a Senior Data/AI Engineer, you will play a central role in building and scaling our data products.
This is not a traditional back-end data engineering role. You will work closely with product, commercial and technical colleagues, transforming datasets into commercial, customer-facing solutions.
You will combine deep technical expertise with a strong understanding of how data can be structured, enriched and operationalised through AI systems.
---
**What You’ll Be Doing**
**Data Product Development (Core Focus)**
* Design and build scalable data products underpinning Beacon’s commercial offerings
* Transform raw and third-party data into structured, enriched, product-ready datasets
* Partner with product and commercial teams to define how data is packaged, accessed and monetised
* Enable delivery via APIs, internal tools and customer-facing platforms
---
**AI & Data Enrichment**
* Apply AI and LLM capabilities to enrich and enhance data (e.g. classification, tagging, summarisation, insight generation)
* Design and build LLM-powered product features
* Integrate RAG into pipelines to improve data quality and unlock new features
* Support development of AI-driven products such as recommendation engines, search and insight tools
* Ensure systems are optimised, well-governed and resilient
---
**Platform & Engineering**
* Support deployment and lifecycle management of data and AI systems
* Own and evolve the data platform architecture (Databricks, Azure, Airbyte) to support scalabilit
* Own performance and cost optimisation across Azure Databricks and supporting Azure services, including compute selection, autoscaling, workload monitoring and resource-efficiency improvements
* Build and maintain robust data pipelines (batch and streaming) delivering reliable, production-ready datasets
* Ensure high standards in data quality, testing and observability
* Improve efficiency through automation, CI/CD and engineering best practice
---
**Commercial & Stakeholder Impact**
* Partner with senior stakeholders to identify high-value data product opportunities
* Translate business needs into practical, scalable data and AI solutions
* Act as a bridge between technical teams and commercial/product stakeholders
* Contribute to prioritisation based on business impact
---
**Leadership & Growth**
* Shape the evolution of our data product and AI strategy
* Mentor junior engineers and promote a strong engineering and product mindset
* Help build a high-performing, commercially aware data and AI engineering team
---
**What We’re Looking For:**
**Core Engineering Experience**
* Deep, hands-on experience designing, building and operating production data platforms using Azure Databricks and Azure Cloud environments
* Strong experience with Apache Spark, PySpark, Spark SQL and Delta Lake, including incremental processing, schema evolution, performance optimisation and batch and streaming workloads.
* Strong experience implementing Unity Catalog, including catalog and schema design, access control, data lineage, discovery and governance of production data assets.
* Proven experience designing lakehouse and Medallion architectures and converting raw and third-party data into governed, reusable data products.
* Advanced Python and SQL, focused on production-quality, scalable solutions
* Proven experience designing and building data pipelines and models
* Experience working with APIs and data delivery mechanisms (critical for productisation)
* Experience deploying Databricks workloads through automated CI/CD, preferably using Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions, automated testing and Databricks Declarative Automation Bundles.
* Experience integrating Azure Databricks with ADLS Gen2, Azure identity, Key Vault, APIs and external data sources.
---
**Data Product Mindset (Key Differentiator)**
* Experience building or supporting data products or customer-facing data solutions
* Strong understanding of how to structure, expose and scale data for end users or clients
* Ability to think beyond pipelines and focus on commercial value
* Experience working closely with product or commercial teams
---
**AI Engineering**

The British Transport Police (BTP) Work Experience Programme gives young people the chance to learn about policing and the many different roles that help keep Britain's railways safe.
You will meet officers, police staff and volunteers from a range of teams and gain an insight into what life is like in a national police force.
Please note that this is an educational work experience programme. Students will **not** carry out operational policing duties and will **not** be placed in active operational environments.
All successful applicants will take part as part of a group and will complete the programme alongside other students.

Job Title: Finance Graduate Programme – Operations and Product Team: Finance Location: Greenford, West London (on site 4 days per week) Reports to: Director of Finance – Operations and Product About the Role Every Brompton bike is designed, engineered and handmade in Greenford. This programme puts you at the heart of the costs, decisions and data behind each one. As Finance’s onsite presence, you will connect Operations and Product teams with offsite finance colleagues, explaining the numbers and bringing back insight from the shop floor. No accounting or business background is needed. We will teach you the finance, support your professional qualification and give you real responsibility from the start. You will also improve processes and data flows, using tools such as SQL, Power Query, Power Automate, ERPs and AI to simplify and automate work.
**What makes this role different**
* On the ground, not behind a screen: You will be based on site, close to the people who design, build and ship our bikes, and close to the decisions that shape them.
* Real impact on our products: Your questions and insights will influence how our products are developed and made. This is at the heart of what we do.
* A pivotal role with many teams: You will work with a variety of Operations and Product teams, as a key onsite finance business partner for colleagues up to Heads of department.
* Learn by doing: You will pick up finance by working on real questions, with the Operations Accountant and Operations Finance Analyst alongside you.
* A modern toolkit: You will use SQL, Power Query and Power Automate, and explore new technologies, to solve problems in creative ways.
* Strong foundations: You will learn why good process, reliable systems and clean data matter, and how to build and improve them.
* A clear route to a professional qualification: We fund and support your CIMA studies, with protected study time at the beginning.
* Direct mentoring: You will report to, and be mentored by, the Director of Finance for Operations & Product.
* A culture of doing more with less: We value frugality, resource efficiency and a genuine commitment to sustainability, and we look for people who enjoy finding smarter ways to work.
**Your development on the programme**
* Year one: You will study the CIMA Certificate in Business Accounting, supported by the company through an apprenticeship. Tuition is covered and you will have protected study time during working hours. You will apply what you learn straight away by supporting the Operations Accountant.
* After the Certificate: The company continues to support you towards the full CIMA qualification, with the aim of completing it within three years. Tuition is covered through the CIMA Finance Leadership Programme.
* Growing responsibility: You will take on more ownership and a wider business partnering role as you progress. Progression in pay and responsibility are part of the programme and linked to your progress with the qualification and your performance on the job over the years.
**Key responsibilities**
**Our finance partner on site**
* Be Finance’s visible, approachable partner for Operations and Product, building trusted relationships across the teams.
* Spend time on the shop floor, in the warehouse and with product teams to understand what is happening and how it affects costs.
* Connect teams with finance colleagues, bringing back the context behind the numbers and answering or directing finance questions.
* Gather key information for budgets, forecasts and projects, and explain costs clearly to non-finance colleagues.
**Supporting the monthly finance cycle**
Support the Operations Accountant with month-end, making sure the costs of building our bikes are recorded accurately and in the right period. You will take on more as your experience grows.
* Help record and understand the parts, consumables and labour that make up the cost of each bike.
* Review product parts lists, production activity and cost implications with the right teams.
* Investigate scrap, freight, duties, warranty claims and other cost movements to understand their causes and impact.
* Support stock checks and keep records of machinery, equipment and tooling accurate.
* Learn how investment in new products, including engineering time and tooling, is recorded over the product’s life.
**Detective work: checks and investigations**
* Complete monthly checks, compare records with independent sources and investigate any differences.
* Trace unusual cost movements to their root cause and clearly record what you checked, found and resolved.
* Help provide the evidence and explanations needed for external audits.
**Improving how we work: process, systems and data**
* Keep finance process guides clear, current and easy to follow.
* Spot slow, manual or error-prone processes and work with teams to improve them.
* Use SQL, Power Query, Power Automate, ERPs and AI to improve data and automate repetitive work.
* Help teams capture accurate information and work with Data & Analytics and Purchase Ledger to improve how it flows into reports.
**The ideal candidate**
**Essential qualifications and experience**
* A bachelor's degree in any subject, recently completed or about to be completed.
* No prior accounting or business studies required: we will teach you.
* An interest in how businesses work and achieve their objectives, and in how teams and organisations interact.
* Comfort with numbers and with Excel.
* The right to work in the UK, and eligibility to start a Level 4 apprenticeship in England (we will help you check this).
* Willingness to be based on site in Greenford, West London, 4 days per week.
* Some experience in data tools such as SQL, Power Query or Power Automate, or any coding, is helpful but not essential, but you need interest and comfort navigating and interrogating data.
**Essential skills and attributes**
* **Analytical mindset:** You break problems down and follow the evidence.
* **Rigour and method:** You are organised, careful and know when good is good enough.
* **Curiosity and investigation:** You keep asking why until you find the real answer.
* **Business acumen:** You are interested in how businesses operate, make money and achieve their goals.

## Opportunity
The Lead Application Security Engineer will join Brunswick's Information Security team and play a key role in shaping how the firm embeds security into application design, development, deployment, and technology change.

Working closely with ICT, AI Engineering, application owners, and business stakeholders, the Lead Application Security Engineer will help define practical security standards, guardrails, review processes, and secure design patterns that enable delivery teams to move at pace while managing risk appropriately.

In this role, you will provide senior application security and DevSecOps expertise across technology projects, design reviews, cloud-based applications, APIs, integrations, delivery pipelines, and selected AI-enabled solutions.
You will act as a senior security advisor to technical and business teams, helping establish a repeatable application security model that can scale as demand grows, including the potential introduction of additional team members in the future.
Key responsibilities include:
* Lead the development of Brunswick's application security capability, including standards, secure design patterns, review processes, and practical guardrails.
* Act as a senior security advisor to ICT, AI Engineering, application owners, and business stakeholders.
* Review and assess application designs, architecture decisions, APIs, integrations, cloud services, and deployment patterns to identify security risks early in the delivery lifecycle.

* Support security assurance activities, including penetration testing, application security testing, remediation tracking, and ensuring appropriate logging, monitoring, and response considerations are built into new solutions.
* Define and document security requirements, architecture decisions, design recommendations, and risk-based remediation actions.
* Support the future growth of the application security function, including helping define ways of working, capability needs, and technical guidance for future team members as the function matures.

OverviewApplication
At Bumble, we’re building the Love Company — a place where healthy, equitable relationships and friendships can start and grow. You’ll lead through technical influence, raise the bar for ML engineering across the organisation, and help us build systems that optimise not simply for engagement, but for better connections and meaningful member outcomes.
### What you'll do
* Define and lead the technical strategy for **AI and Machine Learning systems** that power recommendations, matching, ranking and personalisation across Bumble products, delivering measurable improvements in member outcomes, engagement and safety.
* Design, develop and deploy production-grade models using modern ML frameworks such as **PyTorch**, ensuring scalability, reliability and performance in high-traffic environments.
* Build and deploy production **AI agents** using foundation models and fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs), alongside sub-agents, tools and **MCP integrations**.
* Architect end-to-end ML pipelines, integrating large-scale data processing technologies such as **Spark and Airflow** with model training, evaluation, deployment and monitoring workflows.
* Define and evolve experimentation strategies, including **A/B testing, offline evaluation and online measurement**, to continuously improve model performance and product outcomes.
* Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering and Data leadership to translate complex business and member challenges into impactful ML solutions, collaborating with purpose and influencing at senior levels.
* Mentor and elevate senior individual contributors, fostering a culture of **Excellence, Curiosity and continuous learning** across Bumble’s ML community.
* Take ownership of complex and ambiguous problem spaces, seeing initiatives through from insight to measurable impact whilst adapting approaches as new information emerges.
* Champion **responsible AI practices**, ensuring fairness, transparency, privacy and member safety are considered throughout the design and operation of Machine Learning systems.
### About you
* Typically, you will have **10–15 years of relevant experience**, although we welcome candidates with alternative backgrounds who can demonstrate equivalent skills, scope and impact.
* You have deep expertise in Machine Learning, with significant hands-on experience designing, building and deploying **large-scale ML systems in production environments**.

* You understand modern recommendation-system approaches and can reason deeply about **model architecture, features, loss functions, evaluation methodology, experimentation and the trade-offs between offline performance and online outcomes**.
* You have experience prompting and fine-tuning **Large Language Models (LLMs)** and building production AI agents using modern agentic architectures and tooling.
* You have proven experience designing scalable data and ML pipelines using technologies such as **Spark, Airflow**, or comparable distributed data and orchestration systems.

* You partner effectively across functions, collaborating with purpose and taking ownership of outcomes in complex organisational environments.
* You have a track record of mentoring and developing other engineers, role-modelling **Respect and Excellence** whilst helping build inclusive, high-performing teams.
* You bring strong AI fluency and technical judgement, with the ability to independently design, evaluate and optimise ML systems whilst guiding others in the responsible and effective application of AI.

Bumble Inc. is the parent company of Bumble Date, BFF, and Badoo. The Bumble platform enables people to build healthy and equitable relationships, through Kind Connections. Founded by Whitney Wolfe Herd in 2014, Bumble was one of the first dating apps built with women at the center and connects people across dating (Bumble Date) and friendship (BFF). # Graduate Software Engineer, Open Source and Linux, Canonical Ubuntu
Home based - Worldwide
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.
The company is founder led, profitable and growing.
We are hiring **2025 and 2026 Graduate Software Engineers** into engineering teams around the world. As a global platform company we offer a wide range of software engineering challenges, in both open source products and commercial business systems. We have teams that work in a variety of languages, typically Python, Golang, Rust, C/C++, JavaScript and of course... Bash. We work from the very lowest levels of the Linux system - BIOS and boot loaders, firmware, kernel and drivers, all the way up to desktop applications and containers. We work on tiny devices like the Raspberry Pi and new RISC-V boards, all the way up to supercomputers, clouds and Kubernetes clusters. We work on compilers and toolchains, and we work on security, cryptography, performance and documentation. Some of our teams focus on packaging thousands of pieces of software, others focus on deep contributions to a single body of code.
If you are excited about the potential that open source has for humanity and the enterprise, you have outstanding results in your academic career, and you are excited to contribute to the open source stack, this is the best way to apply to Canonical. We will work with you to identify teams and projects that would be interesting and a good fit for your skills and motivations. The process is highly competitive, it will require effort and excellence to succeed if you apply here.
Most of our engineering teams work from home. We try to align a single team in a single time zone - EMEA (Europe, Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia Pacific and Indian Ocean), and AMER (North, South and Central Americas). Even though you work from home, we try to ensure you always have colleagues alongside to coach and mentor you, and for the companionship of shared problem solving and pair programming. Larger projects have multiple teams and might span the globe. We work with the open source community and specialize in building teams that work well in the 'fishbowl' of open source engineering. This is full time work, five days a week, often solving hard problems with significant responsibility. We don't generally work weekends and nights and we do enjoy good holidays but we also expect productive and intense engagement Monday to Friday.
We bring all our engineering teams together in person twice a year for a deep 'sprint' with other teams to stimulate discussion and enable a wide range of career development paths. * Business and commercial interests

The Role:
At Canopius, our delivery teams are responsible for ensuring that business users
can effectively harness data insights to drive strategic decision making. Our
data strategy is centred around an enterprise Lakehouse platform on Databricks,
avoiding fragmented, ungoverned silos on legacy technologies that hamper
creativity and scalability. We are building a governed, interoperable data
estate that enables self-service for our business teams and provides the trusted
foundation for advanced analytics, machine learning and AI to accelerate change
across our industry.
 
The Data Governance Analyst supports the establishment and operation of
effective data governance across Canopius, helping to ensure data is
well-defined, trusted, controlled and used consistently across the business.
Working within the Data Governance team, the role partners with Data Owners,
Data Stewards and wider governance functions to embed policies, standards,
metadata, lineage, business definitions and data quality practices across all
business domains.
 
The role administers and maintains the Data Governance toolset, ensuring
metadata, business glossary content, data ownership, classifications and
supporting governance artefacts remain accurate, complete and up to date. It
also supports governance forums, working groups, data issue management and
reporting, helping projects and business teams understand and evidence
compliance with data policies and standards.
 
The ideal candidate is an analytical and detail-focused data professional who is
enthusiastic about building a stronger data-led culture and improving the way
data is governed across the organisation. You will bring strong data analysis
and Excel skills, an understanding of data governance principles, and the
confidence to engage stakeholders across business and technology teams. You will
also bring practical experience using governance tooling to support metadata
management, data quality, business glossary maintenance and continuous
improvement. Experience of insurance data, particularly Lloyd's market data,
would be advantageous.

* Support the establishment and ongoing operation of data governance
frameworks, including policies, standards, controls, classifications, and
operating models, across business domains.
* Administer Data Governance tooling and define supporting processes to ensure
metadata, lineage, and business glossary content remain accurate, complete,
and governed.
* Capture, document, and standardise business definitions, key data elements,
and data ownership across domains (e.g., business glossary, data dictionary).
* Support the continuous improvement of the internal Business Glossary
application, capturing business feedback and proposing improvements to ensure
it meets business and governance requirements.
* Collaborate with Data Owners and Data Stewards to develop, document, and
maintain data standards, controls, classifications, and supporting governance
artefacts.
* Monitor adherence to data governance policies, standards, and controls,
supporting compliance and audit activities.
* Provide subject matter expertise on data governance concepts, tools, and best
practices to business and technical stakeholders.
* Contribute to governance forums and working groups, and build strong
relationships across business and technology teams to drive adoption of data
governance practices.
* Promote a data-led culture through training, communications, and engagement
activities relating to data governance, policies, and the Data Governance
roadmap.
* Collate and publish management information on data governance activity,
progress, risks, and outcomes.
* Record, track, and support the management of data incidents, including
associated action plans, the Data Risk Register, and incident logs.
* Work with Data Owners, Data Stewards, Risk, Information Security, Compliance,
and other governance functions to identify, escalate, and resolve data issues
through appropriate governance forums.
* Manage own workload effectively, prioritising activity in line with team,
department, and wider business objectives.
* Undertake other ad-hoc duties as required. 
QUALIFICATIONS
Skills:
 
* Strong practical experience implementing data governance frameworks,
including controls, workflows, and operating models across business domains.
* Experience designing and embedding governance controls into business
processes (e.g. data quality rules, approvals, stewardship workflows).
* Experience supporting data governance tools, with the ability to translate
business feedback into product enhancements that improve usability, adoption,
and alignment to business processes.
* Knowledge of data quality frameworks, controls, and dimensions (accuracy,
completeness, consistency, timeliness).
* Experience defining and documenting business terms, data definitions, and
standards.
* Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work across
business and technical teams (e.g., Data Owners, Data Stewards, Data
Engineering).
* Ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams or operating as a
self-starter, taking ownership of activity and progressing work with minimal
supervision.
* Ability to translate business requirements into governance artefacts and
actionable controls.
* Understanding of regulatory and compliance considerations relating to data
(e.g., PII).
* Strong time-management skills, and attention to detail when managing
metadata, documentation, and governance artefacts.
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with a continuous improvement
mindset.
* Strong Excel and data analysis skills.
* Good communication and presentation skills.
* SQL skills are advantageous.
* Knowledge of Azure DevOps for issue tracking and workflow is advantageous.
* Familiarity with specialty (re)insurance or Lloyd's market data such as
bordereaux, delegated authority, underwriting and claims is advantageous.

* Deep experience designing and engineering security across enterprise networks, devices, identity and access.
* A strong understanding of network segmentation, identity controls and security architecture across cloud systems.
* Hands-on experience implementing identity and access management and privileged-access controls across enterprise identity platforms.

* The ability to create effective security architectures and navigate trade-offs between security, accessibility, decentralisation and performance.

***Purpose of role***
To project manage the Net Zero Carbon programme, ensuring rigour and transparency within Diocesan processes, thereby contributing to the successful outcome. You will bring project management experience and resource to facilitate and serve the programme aims and deliverables.
To support the delivery of environmental sustainability and resilience objectives across the Diocese, including carbon reduction, helping churches and other stakeholders move from vision and assessment through to funded and delivered projects.
***Context and Project Overview***
Following the 2020 General Synod motion to commit to a plan toward being net zero by 2030 the Diocese of Liverpool began its net zero carbon journey by engaging in a programme that was designed to assist our churches, cathedral, diocesan offices, schools, properties and buildings to reduce their carbon footprint. Our programme was evaluated as positive and pioneering in 2025 and has now entered a new phase that requires a project manager and technical lead who can navigate the existing programme toward an integrated alignment with our national church funded Development Investment Programme.
***Key Responsibilities***
The Project Manager and Technical Advisor for Environmental Sustainability and Resilience will focus on five main areas of project development:
1. Offering technical support to churches, cathedral, diocesan offices, schools, properties and buildings to reduce their carbon footprint.
2. Developing and maintaining a pipeline of environmental sustainability and resilience projects, supporting churches and diocesan stakeholders from identification and assessment through to design, funding and implementation.
3. Offering environmental sustainability and resilience advice to the **Diocesan Advisory Committee for the Care of Churches****.**The DAC is a statutory body that advises parishes, Archdeacons, and the diocesan Chancellor on proposed changes, repairs, or reordering of church buildings and churchyards.
4. Providing project technical oversight and management for national church funded Net Zero Carbon Project. This includes:
5. Supporting the delivery of programme outcomes relating to environmental sustainability, Eco Church, Energy Footprint Tool engagement, carbon reduction and wider organisational resilience.
6. Developing and maintaining planning documents for the project in the form of Gantt charts (MS Project), one-page plans etc. Proactively track key actions and outcomes, suggesting interventions where progress is not being made.
7. Developing and maintaining management accounts including forecasting / resource planning.
8. Monitoring programme performance against agreed milestones, budgets, risks and delivery targets, producing clear reports for programme governance and decision-making.
9. Defining measurement criteria / framework for lead and lag goals; ensuring a system is in place for data capture and that it is maintained (definition and process only, data collection by other team members)
10. Developing and maintaining a risk management framework for the project to help highlight areas for particular focus.
11. Supporting the preparation of reports, papers and recommendations for Programme Boards and other governance groups.
12. Ensuring that the team develop a coherent understanding of the stakeholders involved in the programme and execute a strategy to engage with them (managed by the Comms team and Project Officer).
13. Ensuring the project management documents are up to date / available to the Programme Lead for key meetings e.g. the Programme Board.
14. Working alongside our prophetic lead organisation – Faiths4Change – to inspire stakeholders to reduce their carbon footprint, to become environmentally sustainable and future proof their resilience planning. This hearts and minds culture change work is required at every level of the organisation and across all programmes.
15. Fundraising and fund management: whilst we are not looking for someone to directly fundraise, we do need the postholder to work on tenders and bids that will ensure the long-term sustainability and resilience of the project. This will involve contributing to the writing of bids, using data-analysis to measure impact and social value and working alongside colleagues in identifying, seeking and securing appropriate funding streams. There will also be an element of fund management as we disseminate small grants.
The post holder will undertake other relevant duties as may be requested from time to time and commensurate with the role.

## Talent Acquisition Manager
**Location:** Hybrid remote/Aldgate, London. 1-3 days per week onsite **Salary:** £75,000-£90,000 **SC Clearance Requirements:**
Due to working with several government bodies, SC clearance is required for this position. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but **you must be eligible to pass SC clearance**.
You **must be UK-based**.
## At a glance
This isn’t a desk to run from the sidelines. You’ll build a team of five, and you’ll carry a quota alongside them, because the fastest way to earn a recruiter’s trust is to be in the market doing the job yourself.
## The moment
Cloudscaler is 130 people today, heading to 170 by the end of this year and roughly double again across 2027. Every one of those hires has to come through a Talent Acquisition function that is being rebuilt, not simply inherited.
You’re backfilling a role, but not into the same role. We’re changing the shape of it: less oversight from a distance, more hands directly in the market, and a team built around you from close to a standing start.
We’ve leaned on agencies to cover gaps in the past, and it hasn’t delivered what it should have. That’s part of why this role exists: to build an internal team good enough that we need agencies far less.
## What makes this different
Most Talent Acquisition Manager roles are one step removed from the desk. You review pipeline in a dashboard, chase recruiters for updates and step in only when something stalls. That’s not this.
* Rather than managing a desk from a distance, you’ll carry your own requisitions alongside the team.
* Rather than reviewing pipeline after the fact, you’ll build the direct-sourcing pipeline yourself, in the toughest markets.
* Rather than outsourcing hard roles to agencies, you’ll own the reduction in agency spend, personally.
* Rather than inheriting a settled team, you’ll build a team of five from close to zero.
**To be clear about the level: this is a player-manager role, not a strategic seat one step back from delivery. You’ll fill roles yourself while you build and coach the team around you. That combination is the job, not a phase you grow out of.**
## The role
You’ll lead Talent Acquisition, reporting to the Chief People Officer, with three to five Talent Acquisition Partners reporting to you from day one. You’ll personally own the senior, technical and business-critical hires, while building your team’s capability, capacity and direct-sourcing discipline underneath you.
Two things define the job. The first is delivery: you carry your own quota and remain close enough to the market that you can spot a stalled pipeline or a shifting candidate expectation before it becomes a missed hire. The second is building: assembling a team from close to scratch, giving each Partner a vertical to own, and instilling a direct-sourcing-first culture rather than a dependency on agencies and job boards.
## Where the role starts and stops
New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today.
**Yours:** Full-cycle recruitment delivery and team leadership. Personally leading senior, technical and business-critical hires. Building and coaching Talent Acquisition Partners. Ashby ownership and data quality. Direct-sourcing strategy and capability. Agency relationships, spend and the plan to reduce reliance on them. Cost-per-hire and pipeline reporting.
**Shared:** The handover from offer to start date, which the People Partner team picks up for onboarding and clearance. Early careers programmes, which a Talent Acquisition Partner will own day to day with your oversight. Broader People systems architecture, which sits with the CPO.
**Not yours:** Employee relations casework, onboarding delivery and clearance coordination, which sit with the People Partner team. The design of the wider People strategy and operating model, which sits with the CPO.
## The stack
You won’t be handed a settled toolkit and told to leave it alone. Part of the job is making these systems earn their keep.
* **Ashby:** Our applicant tracking system, and yours to own. Workflows, pipeline stages, reporting and data quality all sit with you, for your whole team.
* **Metaview:** Interview intelligence, feeding into how you quality-assure interviews and coach the team’s technique.
* **Rippling:** The single source of truth for the employee record. You’ll work in it from offer through to handover and lean on its reporting for headcount and cost-per-hire data.
* **Claude:** Cloudscaler is an Anthropic partner. You’ll use it daily for role briefs, market mapping, candidate communication and case preparation.
## What you’ll do
**Carry your own quota.** You’ll personally lead recruitment for our most senior, technical and business-critical roles, staying close enough to the market to spot problems before they cost a hire.
**Build the team.** You’ll grow Talent Acquisition to three to five Partners, giving each one a technical vertical to own and coaching them from requisition to offer.
**Make direct sourcing the default.** You’ll lead our Sourcing First approach in practice, not on a slide, building your own pipelines and teaching your team to do the same.
**Reduce agency reliance.** You’ll manage the agency relationships that remain, hold them to account, and shrink the spend as your internal pipeline strengthens.
**Own the numbers.** Cost per hire, time to fill, pipeline health and Ashby data quality are yours to report on, and yours to improve.
**Back early careers.** You’ll give a Talent Acquisition Partner room to build our graduate and apprentice pipeline, with your steer on shape and priority.
**Use AI properly.** You’ll use Claude and Metaview to take routine work off your desk and your team’s, so more of the week goes on the market and the people in it.
## What success looks like at 12 months
* Your team is at full strength (three to five Partners), and each owns a vertical with a live direct-sourcing pipeline.
* Cost-per-hire, time-to-hire and quality-of-hire have moved in the right direction, and agency spend is materially down.
* Senior and business-critical roles are closing without stalling in interview or offer.
* Ashby data is clean enough that pipeline reporting can be trusted without checking it first.
* An early careers cohort has been hired and started, owned day-to-day by one of your Partners.
* Hiring leaders come to you with a problem, not a job description, because they trust the process.
## Who we’re looking for
**A full-cycle recruiter at heart.** You’ve carried a quota and closed hard roles yourself, and you’re not looking to leave that behind for a purely oversight role.
**A genuine direct sourcer.** You build pipelines rather than waiting for applications, and you can teach that skill to others.
**A first-time or early people manager, or ready to be one.** You want to build and coach a small team, not just manage a desk.
**Credible in technical markets.** You can hold a real conversation with engineering and cloud hiring leaders about what good looks like.
**Data-literate.** You’re comfortable owning cost-per-hire and pipeline reporting yourself, not waiting for someone else to produce it.
**Comfortable rebuilding, not just running.** This team is being reshaped, not inherited whole. You’ll enjoy the first six months more than most people would.
## The honest part
You’re inheriting a function that needs rebuilding, including some agency relationships that haven’t delivered and a team that doesn’t exist yet at full strength. That means real early weeks spent both recruiting for your own roles and recruiting your own team.

SHREDDER addresses a critical separation challenge in UK lithium-ion battery recycling: current mechanical shredding processes produce mixed "black mass" in which graphite and metals are contaminated and difficult to separate, resulting in significant loss of recoverable material value. * Investigate closed-loop wet shredding processes and additive use to promote graphite delamination from cathode active material and metal fractions
* Characterise shredded cell components, black mass, and separated fractions, including establishing and operating new ICP-OES, SEM, XRD and XRF analytical capability
* Generate validated datasets linking shredding parameters to graphite yield, purity, and downstream metal fraction quality, for translation into industrial-scale design by MTC
* Collaborate closely with MTC and Ecobat to support translation of laboratory findings into deployable industrial processes
