# Research Fellow: ESRC Project 'Accent Bias and Domestic Abuse Victimisation (ABDAVic)
> Research Fellow: ESRC Project 'Accent Bias and Domestic Abuse Victimisation (ABDAVic)
The department of Languages, Cultures and Linguistics (LCL) at the University of Southampton has a strong research culture covering a broad range of linguistics disciplines, including but not limited to sociolinguistics, applied linguistics, language acquisition, corpus linguistics, and language education. In addition to our linguistics contingent, LCL is also home to researchers engaging in cultural and area studies linked to the languages taught in the department including French, Spanish, German and Portuguese.
The advertised role is a fixed-term 12-month research-only position supporting the project 'Accent Bias and Domestic Abuse Victimisation (ABDVic)', funded by an ESRC New Investigator grant and led by principal investigator Dr Matthew Hunt. The ABDAVic project is an experimental sociolinguistics project aimed at uncovering possible linguistic discrimination of domestic abuse victims, with a specific focus on biases against classed and racialised accents. The project will involve two stages. Stage One will involve conducting matched guise-style experiments with members of the general population, while Stage Two will involve conducting those same experiments with trained domestic abuse support workers. The role is primarily to support design and implementation of these experiments - including creating auditory stimuli - as well as analysis and dissemination of the results. This role can be optionally completed remotely, with the occasional visit to Southampton or travel for conferences.
Applicants will be expected to be proficient in survey design and implementation, ideally with the university's approved survey tool Qualtrics. They will also be expected to be proficient in either R or Python for statistical analysis, including data visualisation and mixed effect regression. They will also make written contributions to conference abstracts and talks, and eventual journal articles stemming from the project; at least one of these articles will feature the research assistant as lead author. While this is a sociolinguistics project, the position is open to applicants with PhDs in experimental social research more broadly, including applicants from fields like sociology, psychology and political science. Applicants with experience working in the areas of language and ethnicity and/or language and social class are preferred. Experience in phonetics and proficiency in Praat and Audacity is also desirable.

The mindset is the engine, and it is almost impossible to teach retrospectively. You are outcome obsessed, not output obsessed and you care whether the problem was actually solved - you resist the ego instinct to admire a clever solution and ask whether it was needed at all.
You are intellectually honest about uncertainty, taking a trust-but-verify approach and assuming the surprising bug is the one that will burn. You are deeply pragmatic, which matters at CreateFuture where pace counts: you have outgrown the religious wars about platforms, languages and patterns, you hold opinions loosely, and you decide for the systems in front of you, not the ones you wish you had.
You have a bias toward delivery: the smallest thing that works, then iterate, treating documents and meetings as means to that end.

## **AI as the accelerant**
For a Principal to be truly exceptional, this is now already a first-class competency in your arsenal, not a side skill. An engineer who is brilliant by last year's standards but not fluent with AI is not exceptional in 2026. In practice that means:
* **Setting AI up to succeed.** You treat context engineering as a craft (the right files, specs, examples and constraints), and you architect systems with clean interfaces, good naming, machine-readable specs and knowledge bases so the codebase is a quality baseline AI can work on later. No separate ivory-tower architect required.
* **Reviewing and choosing well.** You read far more code than you write, and your value is in the quality of review: catching the silent assumption, the security flaw, the architectural drift, knowing where models fail and looking there first. You pick the right tool for the job (Claude Code for a deep refactor, an inline assistant when that is enough, a sub-agent for parallel work, the right model for analysis versus generation) and you know the constraints differ by client, an enterprise like PayPoint or Natwest versus a scale-up type business like Zuto or OAG.
* **Working with non-determinism.** You see where AI moves the bottleneck and help people left and right of you unblock the value stream. You build with AI components but know success is no longer a binary, reaching for evals, golden datasets, structured outputs and fallback paths as naturally as you reach for unit tests.
## **Technical breadth across the full stack**
Exceptional means depth in at least one area but competence everywhere the system reaches.
* **Backend:** an instinct for distributed systems (what fails, what is eventually consistent, where queues back up), APIs that age well, thoughtful data modelling, and an understanding that languages are mostly syntax differences you can close with AI.
* **Cloud:** cost-aware and security-aware by default, reaching for IaC, composing the primitives rather than stitching together managed services and hoping it works.
* **Data:** modern pipelines, governance and lineage, increasingly vector stores and embeddings, with data quality treated as seriously as production code because garbage in, garbage out is far worse once AI features depend on it.
* **Web and mobile:** past the framework arguments, with a clear view on what you would pick today, and able to build "good enough" front ends yourself with AI.
Full-stack here means seeing the platform as one system and knowing which levers matter most. It does not mean front-end work with a few Node.js servers.
### ## **System thinking, consulting and commercial judgement**
At CreateFuture we work in a consultancy context, where many otherwise excellent IC engineers can struggle.
You know technology is roughly 30% of the picture; the rest is design, argument and reasoning, commercial and political acumen, and the clarity to frame outcomes for a COO, CTO, CIO or CEO in their own language.
You know when gold-plating is wasteful, you can name when a project's real problem is not technical and say so even when it is awkward, and you have a strong sense of what is durable versus what is fashion.
You are not the engineer who introduced the team to seven new technologies last year; you are the one who removed three and quietly made the remaining stack stronger.
## **Leadership mentality**
Technical work is necessary but no longer sufficient. By default you raise the level of everyone around you, regardless of discipline.
* Communicate clearly and frequently (documents, decisions, post-mortems, design notes); the written artefact is the machine-readable context we can feed to AI later.
* Make decisions and own them. You don't escalate everything or hoard control, and you are willing to be the benevolent dictator when it is your turn.
* Mentor in AI fluency, not just code: tooling, prompting and review discipline, so your team is twice as productive a year from now.
* Need little line management. You communicate upwards, raise by exception, self-resolve, and can be trusted with financial controls.
* Disagree well. You tell people they are wrong with evidence and no ego, and you change your own mind when you are shown to be wrong.
## **What we're not looking for**
* The gifted engineer who sits in a silo. This is a team game.
* The one who is fluent with AI but ships without the guardrails and quality gates enterprise clients expect.
* The one with strong technical opinions who cannot justify them commercially and gets defensive when challenged.
* The pure manager who wants to orchestrate teams rather than get involved. This is about setting a new standard, not coordinating it.
* The engineer who will not immerse in a client environment. This role will mean on-site work and trusted relationships built in person. We are not going back to working away from the client and being bypassed.

That means combining graphic design, visual research, photography, film, typography, storytelling and world-building—often delivering a finished presentation within just a few days.
We’re a small, busy team, so you won’t spend your first year sitting on the sidelines. You’ll work alongside experienced creatives, contribute to real projects and see how work develops from the first conversation through to final delivery.

## The role
At the heart of this role are two things: finding exceptional visual references and ideas, and presenting them effectively.
You’ll work closely with our creative team to interpret briefs, discover brilliant visual references and turn ideas into compelling, beautifully designed presentations.
One day you might be researching cinematic night photography for a car commercial; the next you could be exploring authentic casting references in New York, extraordinary rainforest locations, a specific camera technique, or the visual world for a comedy, fashion or technology film.
You’ll then help bring those ideas together through typography, layout and imagery. It’s varied, creative and often fast-moving.

* Use design and layout to strengthen the director’s ideas rather than simply decorate them.
* Respond quickly and accurately to creative feedback.
* Maintain a consistently high visual standard across detailed presentations.
* Quality-check copy, imagery, layouts, links and exports before delivery.
* Maintain exceptionally organised working files.

* Explore new approaches to treatments and digital presentations.
* Experiment with emerging creative and AI tools.
* Contribute to HSS’s website, portfolio, branding and creative output.

* Motion design or video editing

Can you explain how to assemble something without using a single word? That’s the heart of this role.
We’re working with a leading design-led brand in the luxury interiors sector to find a Technical Designer/Illustrator to join their R&D team. Founded in the late 1990s and still driven by the same design philosophy, they’ve grown from a British start-up into a globally recognised name, with products now selling in over 90 countries and established subsidiaries in the US and Asia.
It’s a business built on craftsmanship, precision and the belief that good design demands simplicity — and that thinking extends all the way to the documentation that goes in the box.
## The Role
You’ll create clear, step-by-step diagrammatic installation instructions for new and existing products, taking a design from engineering data through to the finished guide a customer or installer actually uses. You’ll also generate product markings for compliance purposes.
Because these products ship to over 90 countries, the instructions have to work without language. The skill is figuring out how to communicate a sequence—order, orientation, which way a part turns, what “done” looks like—purely through images. The creativity is in the problem-solving, not the visual flourish.
Most product imagery is generated in SolidWorks Composer and then brought together in Adobe InDesign and Illustrator, with some illustration created directly within the Adobe suite. You’ll also work with a bespoke Product Lifecycle Management system.
You’ll report to the Technical Manager and work closely with product development engineers, but you’ll manage your own workload against product launch deadlines — so this suits someone organised and self-directed who can keep multiple launches moving at once.
## Being Straight With You
This isn’t a fancy creative design role. If you’re looking for brand work, campaigns or a portfolio full of visual showpieces, this won’t be the one. What it is: a genuinely satisfying craft, where success is measured by someone opening a box and getting it right the first time, without ever reaching for words.
You do still need a good eye. Layout, hierarchy, consistency and clarity all matter enormously here — they’re just in service of comprehension rather than aesthetics.
## What We’re Looking For
We’re open on background. You could already be doing this exact job, or you could be coming from an adjacent role and looking for something different:
* Someone already producing sequential assembly or installation instructions
* A technical illustrator, CAD technician or artworker wanting a change of direction

## What matters most:
* The ability to communicate a physical process through images alone
* A strong eye for clarity, sequence and simplicity
* Confidence with Adobe InDesign and/or SolidWorks (SolidWorks Composer experience is a real advantage, but we’ll consider people keen to learn it)
* Comfortable working from engineering data and collaborating with development engineers

Boomkat is looking for an experienced multidisciplinary designer and photographer to join our small team in Manchester.
This is not a graduate or entry-level position. We're looking for someone with substantial professional experience who can work confidently and independently across photography, moving image and graphic design, combining strong technical ability with excellent visual judgement, accuracy and an understanding of the demands of commercial work.
It's an unusual combination of disciplines, so we're less concerned with your current job title than with the quality of your work, your experience and the ideas you can bring to the role.
## About us
Established in Manchester in 1998, Boomkat is an independent online record store specialising in innovative, exceptional and often overlooked music from around the world.
Alongside the store, we work closely with artists and labels and are involved in releasing and presenting music across vinyl, CD, cassette and digital formats.
Physical objects and how they are presented have always been an important part of what we do. We care about photography, typography, record sleeves, print, film and the wider visual culture surrounding music, and we're looking for someone who shares those interests.
## Where we're heading
We've recently launched a completely redesigned Boomkat website, and this role comes at a point when we want to make a similar step forward in the visual work surrounding it.
We have an established photographic style and a strong sense of what Boomkat is, but we're not looking for someone simply to maintain what already exists. We want to improve and develop how we photograph the things we sell, considerably raise the ambition of our moving-image work, and bring more creative thinking to the way Boomkat and the music we care about are presented visually.
We're looking for someone who will take an active part in that process — bringing their own ideas, references and experience, questioning things when they can be better, and helping us work out what the next version of Boomkat's visual language should look like.
## The role
A significant part of the role is photography.
You'll be responsible for photographing the records, books, tapes and other physical releases that appear on Boomkat. We have an established in-house photographic style and a high standard of consistency and accuracy, so you'll need to be able to understand and work confidently within that from the outset.
At the same time, we don't want things to stand still. We're looking for someone with the experience and imagination to develop that visual language, experiment with new approaches and bring strong ideas of their own.
Moving image is increasingly important to us. We want to develop a much stronger and more distinctive approach to video around the music and physical releases we sell and release ourselves.
This includes shooting and editing short-form work for social media and our website , but we're less interested in simply producing "content" than in finding interesting and visually distinctive ways of presenting music and physical objects through moving image. We want the person joining us to play an important part in shaping what that looks like.
You'll also work on graphic design projects, particularly artwork and layouts for vinyl, cassette and CD releases, alongside occasional work across other areas of Boomkat.
A sophisticated understanding of typography and layout is essential.
This is a creative design position rather than a production-artworking or pre-press role. Technical preparation of finished artwork for manufacture isn't part of the job.
## Experience
We're looking for somebody who already has significant professional experience in photography and visual design.
You should be comfortable working in a commercial environment where deadlines are real, details matter and work needs to be delivered accurately and consistently.
You'll need to be capable of managing your own workload, prioritising competing requirements and taking a project from brief through to a finished piece of work without requiring constant supervision.
We're deliberately not specifying an exact number of years of experience. The quality and breadth of someone's professional work matters more to us than whether they've been doing it for five years or ten.
However, this isn't a position intended for recent graduates or someone looking for their first professional creative role.
## What we're looking for
We're looking for somebody with strong visual judgement and cultural awareness as well as technical ability.
You might currently be a photographer who also designs and works with moving image; a multidisciplinary designer with particularly strong photography skills; or somebody whose career has naturally moved between these disciplines.
We're looking for:
* Excellent professional photography skills, including a strong understanding of lighting, composition, colour and image processing.
* Professional experience producing photography to a consistently high standard and to deadline.
* Strong moving-image skills, including shooting and editing, and an interest in developing ideas rather than simply reproducing established social-media formats.
* Strong graphic-design skills, with typography and layout being particularly important.
* Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
* The ability to work quickly when necessary without allowing standards to slip.
* A high level of visual and cultural awareness.
* Confidence with the relevant Adobe Creative Cloud, Final Cut and other relevant applications and professional photographic/video equipment.
* The ability to understand and work within an established visual language while also finding intelligent ways of developing it.
* The confidence and experience to work independently, make good visual decisions and take responsibility for projects.
* Ideas. We want somebody who notices things, brings references to the table, does research, suggests possibilities and contributes creatively rather than simply waiting to be given instructions.
An interest in music is important, but we're equally interested in the wider culture that informs your work — photography, film, books, magazines, fashion, contemporary art, independent publishing, typography and design.
We don't necessarily expect one person to be equally accomplished in every discipline. You might, for example, be an exceptional photographer and designer with somewhat less professional moving-image experience. What matters is that your portfolio demonstrates an exceptional visual eye, genuine ability across disciplines and the potential to develop the areas in which you're less experienced.
## Portfolio
A strong portfolio is essential and must be submitted with your application.
We will use portfolios to select candidates for interview, so please make sure yours gives us a good understanding of both the quality and breadth of your work.
In particular, we'd like to see examples of:
* Photography you've conceived and shot yourself.
* Commercial/product or still-life photography where relevant.
* Moving-image work you've shot and/or directed and edited.
* Graphic design demonstrating strong typography and layout.
* Projects where you've developed an idea or visual approach rather than simply executed somebody else's direction.
Please make your own contribution to collaborative projects clear.
We're interested in the finished work, but also in seeing evidence of judgement, consistency and ideas. A small, carefully selected portfolio of excellent work is considerably more useful to us than a very large collection of everything you've ever made.
## Working at BoomKat
This is a permanent, studio-based position in Manchester for three or four days per week.
Because photography, physical products and working directly with the rest of the team are fundamental to the role, the position is entirely on-site. There is no remote or hybrid working option.
We're deliberately open to either three or four days. This may suit an established creative who wants to retain some time for their own practice or selected freelance work alongside a permanent position.
The full-time equivalent salary is £42,000–£48,000, depending on experience, paid pro rata according to the agreed working pattern.
We're a small independent company, which means this role comes with considerable creative involvement. Good ideas don't have to pass through multiple layers of management: we're looking for somebody experienced enough to contribute them and capable enough to make them happen.
## How to apply
Please send your application to jobs@boomkat.com including the following:
* A link to your portfolio.
* A considered cover letter explaining why you're interested in this particular position and why you think you'd be a good fit for Boomkat.
* Your CV, including relevant professional experience.
* Whether you're interested in working three or four days per week.
* Your current availability / notice period.
* Tell us about one piece of visual work - by anyone - that you've seen recently and thought was exceptional, and briefly tell us why. It could be photography, a film, a record sleeve, a book, an exhibition, a piece of graphic design or something else entirely. There isn't a right answer: we're interested in what catches your attention and how you think about visual work.
Both a portfolio and cover letter are required for an application to be considered.
We take the cover letter seriously. We're interested in applicants who have taken the time to understand what Boomkat does and have thought specifically about why this role and this company interest them.
Applications consisting of a generic CV or covering letter without a relevant portfolio won't be considered.
Please send your application, portfolio and CV to jobs@boomkat.com with “Multidisciplinary Designer / Photographer” in the subject line.

# Head of Product Marketing & Growth
Global - Remote
**About Defuse Labs**
Defuse Labs builds NEAR Intents, the universal transaction layer for the AI economy — intent-based infrastructure that enables people, agents, and applications to move value across chains and assets without bridges, fragmented liquidity, or manual routing.
At the center of our product ecosystem is **near.com**.
**near.com** is building a permissionless financial account: one place to hold, grow, invest, trade and use assets across blockchains, with privacy and control at its core. Our ambition is to make sophisticated financial capabilities feel like parts of one coherent product, increasingly accessible through conversation and trusted agents.
Our initial customers are comfortable with crypto and value their time, privacy and independence. They want access to what financial technology makes possible without having to manage its complexity.
We also build **NEAR Intents**, the universal transaction layer for the AI economy — intent-based infrastructure that enables people, agents, and applications to move value across chains and assets without bridges, fragmented liquidity, or manual routing. Instead of specifying a transaction path, users simply express what they want to achieve, and a competitive network of solvers fulfills the intent with competitive execution across available liquidity.
*We operate in startup mode: high ownership, fast execution, and high standards. We’re a small, globally distributed team that moves quickly, takes initiative, and adapts as the product and market evolve.*
**About the Role**
We’re hiring a **Head of Product Marketing & Growth (Lead)** with a primary focus on **near.com** — owning how the product is positioned, understood, launched, and adopted by users.
This is a foundational, highly product-oriented role responsible for **how near.com is understood, brought to market, and adopted by users**. You’ll develop a deep understanding of our users and market, define the product’s positioning, target audiences and core use cases, and own go-to-market across launches and the broader product lifecycle.
You’ll work closely with Product and Growth to turn that understanding into adoption — shaping onboarding, messaging, distribution and product education, and identifying the barriers that prevent users from discovering value and coming back. You’ll combine qualitative customer insight with product data to understand what resonates, where users drop off, and what could improve acquisition, activation, engagement and retention.
This is not a role that simply markets what Product has already built. You’ll bring the market and user perspective into product decisions, helping us determine **who we are building for, which use cases matter most, how the product should evolve, and how we take it to market**.
You’ll also support product marketing for **NEAR Intents**, particularly around partner positioning, integrations, and launches with CEXs, wallets, fintech platforms, and other distribution partners.
You’ll be particularly effective in this role if you’ve worked and grew the consumer product organization at a CEX, fintech company, neo-banks, wallet, trading platform, payments product, or another digital-asset business. You understand how users discover and evaluate financial or crypto products, what creates trust and friction, and how product experience, positioning, onboarding and distribution work together to drive adoption.

# Bibliographic Metadata and ONIX Feeds Manager – DK Digital Product
Company:

# Job Description
Are you interested in bibliographic metadata and the systems that support digital publishing?
DK is looking for a Bibliographic Metadata and ONIX Feeds Manager to join our global publishing operations team. This role ensures accurate bibliographic metadata reaches retailers, libraries and data aggregators worldwide. Our ONIX feeds communicate information about DK’s books and support their sale and distribution.
You’ll manage DK’s ONIX feeds, monitor their performance, investigate issues and ensure they meet industry standards, legal requirements and business needs. You’ll create new feeds, update existing ones and work with internal teams and external data recipients to ensure metadata is delivered accurately.
You’ll also advise and train colleagues on metadata standards and best practice, lead work to improve data quality, particularly subject classification, and contribute to projects that improve our systems, data flows and processes.
We’re looking for someone with experience working with ONIX and bibliographic metadata, ideally within publishing or the wider book industry. You’ll have experience using Biblio or an equivalent bibliographic database, strong Excel skills and a methodical approach to problem-solving. Attention to detail is essential, as is an interest in improving quality, accuracy and efficiency.
Knowledge of BISAC and/or Thema subject classification schemes would be useful. Experience delivering training, writing documentation, or specifying and testing database functionality would also be an advantage.
Key responsibilities
* Monitor DK’s ONIX feeds, ensuring they run reliably and metadata is delivered accurately to external partners
* Investigate and resolve feed issues, making adjustments to meet internal requirements, external specifications and industry standards
* Create new feeds and update existing feeds as systems, partners and business needs change
* Improve the quality of DK’s bibliographic metadata, advising and training colleagues on standards and best practice
* Work on projects to improve data flows, bibliographic systems and processes
* Work with colleagues in Audio, Sales, publishing divisions, Digital and Sales Operations in Delhi, and PRH UK and US
* Communicate with external data recipients and take part in industry working groups
Essential skills
* Experience working with ONIX feeds and bibliographic metadata, preferably within publishing, bookselling, libraries, wholesaling, distribution or a related organisation.
* Experience monitoring, investigating and resolving data or feed errors, including identifying causes and taking action to resolve or prevent recurrence.
* Experience creating, updating or testing data feeds, feed configurations or similar system outputs to meet changing business, system or partner requirements.
* Experience using a bibliographic database or product information system, with an understanding of how metadata flows between internal systems and external recipients, and the ability to use Excel to review and analyse data.
* Knowledge of bibliographic metadata standards, together with the ability to improve data quality and explain technical processes or requirements clearly through advice, training or documentation.
At DK, you’ll join a small team supporting a complex publishing operation. The role covers a wide range of work, giving you the opportunity to influence how our digital supply chain operates. You’ll use specialist systems and processes and develop an understanding of how bibliographic data is created, managed and distributed across the book industry.
This role could suit someone with experience in publishing, bookselling, libraries, wholesaling or distribution who wants to improve the data that helps DK’s books reach readers.
Working from the office a minimum of three days a week, you’ll join a supportive team. If you’re interested in metadata quality, problem-solving and improving processes, we encourage you to apply.

DK is looking for a Digital Supply Chain Coordinator to join our global publishing operations team. This is a key role at the heart of our digital publishing process, ensuring our ebooks reach retailers worldwide on time, in the right format, and with flawless metadata. If you enjoy unravelling challenges, working with large datasets, and spotting and fixing issues before they become problems, this could be the perfect role for you.
In this role, you’ll be the link between our publishing teams, technology providers, and retail partners, monitoring data feeds between our systems and online retailers, swiftly investigating and resolving any issues. You’ll upload and deliver ebook files, keep our catalogues accurate through regular audits, and respond to queries from across the business. You’ll also coordinate data releases to align with key announcements.
We’re looking for someone highly organised and resilient under pressure, with exceptional attention to detail and clear, confident communication skills. You’ll have experience working with large datasets in Excel or Google Sheets and a methodical approach to problem solving. Knowledge of systems such as Biblio and CoreSource, ONIX metadata, or experience liaising with retailers would be an advantage, but most important is your technical aptitude, curiosity, and willingness to learn.
Key responsibilities:
* Coordinate the supply of ebooks through complex distribution channels, meeting deadlines and industry standards
* Act as the central communication hub between internal teams and external partners, ensuring clarity on file delivery, metadata, and processes
* Perform regular checks on metadata and files, maintain accurate catalogues, and resolve ingestion or distribution errors
* Identify bottlenecks, implement efficiencies, and document best practices to improve workflows
* Build strong relationships with digital partners to meet their distribution needs and uphold DK’s reputation for excellence
At DK, you’ll work with digital products that reach millions of readers, collaborate with passionate colleagues, and help shape processes that make a lasting impact. You’ll be involved in every stage, from initial file delivery through to publication, gaining a holistic view of how digital books are produced and delivered. This is an excellent opportunity for someone eager to make a meaningful impact in digital publishing and to play a crucial role in delivering DK’s award‐winning content to a worldwide audience.
Working from the office a minimum of three days a week, you’ll join a supportive, collaborative team environment. If you are motivated by process, efficiency, and precision, we encourage you to apply.
To apply, please submit your most recent CV and cover letter by midnight on 11th January 2026.
Salary: up to £30,000 depending on how your skills and experience align to the role, plus bonus and benefits
Closing date for applications: 18th October 2026.

**Fundamental Researcher - Compute Markets**
**The role**
* DRW Asset Management is seeking a Fundamental Researcher to develop investment views on compute markets and the infrastructure that supports them. You will research the economics of compute supply and demand, form views on the macro forces shaping the market, and translate them into investment recommendations for a compute derivatives strategy.
* You will work alongside a quantitative researcher who owns the pricing models. Your contribution is an independent, fundamental perspective: understanding the models well enough to test their assumptions against what is happening in the market, and flagging when the market has moved ahead of them.
* This is a founding seat on a small investment team. We are particularly interested in candidates with credit, commodities or semiconductor research experience who can apply rigorous analysis of cash flows, capacity, contracts and downside risk to a market that is still taking shape. We do not expect deep prior experience in compute. We expect strong analytical foundations and the curiosity to build sector expertise quickly.
* What you'll do
* Develop macro and fundamental views on compute. Track and interpret the forces driving supply and demand: AI training and inference demand, hyperscaler and neocloud capital expenditure, chip supply and generational transitions, data center capacity, power availability, financing conditions and policy, including export controls.
* Translate pricing into investment views. Assess what compute pricing across contract terms and chip generations implies about demand, capacity and scarcity. Identify where prices diverge from fundamentals and recommend how to express those views.
* Validate pricing assumptions. Develop a working understanding of the pricing models and supply the fundamental evidence behind their key inputs, including supply pipeline, utilization, workload mix and the pace of price declines across hardware generations. Challenge those inputs when the evidence changes.
* Build research models. Develop supply-and-demand balances, unit economics and scenarios that connect fundamental drivers to compute pricing and investment outcomes, with assumptions documented and testable.
* Assess counterparties and assets with a credit investor's discipline. Evaluate revenue quality, utilization, cost structure, customer concentration, contractual commitments, leverage, liquidity and refinancing risk. Examine how generational turnover and the falling cost of compute affect asset values, counterparty resilience and recoveries.
* Make clear recommendations. Present to the Portfolio Manager and Investment Committee, setting out the investment thesis, valuation framework, catalysts, risks and the evidence that would change the view.
* Build differentiated information sources. Develop a network of industry contacts and data sources across hardware, cloud, data center and power markets to test assumptions and spot inflections early.
**What we're looking for**
* 5 to 7 years of fundamental investment research experience, ideally in credit research or investing (including structured or asset-backed finance), commodities (particularly power and energy), or buy-side or sell-side coverage of semiconductors and digital infrastructure.
* A demonstrated ability to turn complex or incomplete information into a clear investment judgment.
* Strong financial modeling skills and a thorough understanding of cash flow analysis, capital structures and downside scenarios.
* Enough quantitative fluency to engage with pricing models: understand how they work, interrogate their inputs and judge whether their outputs are consistent with the market. You will not be expected to build or maintain them.
* An understanding of how a fundamental view translates into a derivatives position such as a forward or swap, or the ability to learn this quickly.
* The ability to distinguish structural trends from temporary supply-and-demand imbalances and to assess what is already reflected in pricing.
* A strong interest in compute markets and the drive to build expertise across hardware, cloud services, data centers and power infrastructure. Prior experience in the sector is valuable but not required.
* Clear written and verbal communication, intellectual independence, and a willingness to challenge assumptions and revise views as evidence changes.

**Purpose of Job**
EBRD’s engagement with donors has increased in both scale and depth in recent years with more than 50 multilateral and bilateral donors currently supporting the organisation, and close to two thirds of the Bank’s investments now drawing on donor support. Donor support, in the form of grants and blended finance for investments, advisory services or policy reform, has become an integral part of EBRD’s business model and crucial to help the Bank deliver on its transition mandate. At the same time, the effective use of concessional finance and blended finance requires ensuring that such support enhances the impact of EBRD investments, addresses market failures and does not distort markets, in line with relevant DFI principles for blended finance.
This post plays an important role in helping to shape EBRD’s donor agenda and strategic relations with its growing donor community as the Bank expands into new regions and embarks on a new Strategic and Capital Framework period (2026-2030). The Associate Director will establish effective and impactful strategies, policies and related guidelines for the Bank’s broader donor agenda. The post holder also leads on analysing global development and blended finance trends and bring this knowledge to the Bank and will lead the Blended Finance Team in the Impact & Partnership Group of the Bank. This involves having a good understanding of both the Bank’s donor support needs and donor priorities, as well as how blended finance can address market failures and enhance the impact and additionality of the Bank’s investments. The role also includes producing a variety of analysis and financial data to capture the Bank’s use and impact of donor resources and blended finance structures, including their contribution to addressing market failures and achieving development impact, and communicating this through an array of products and events to both internal and external audiences.
The post straddles two teams – Donor Partnerships and Impact – and the post holder will lead a team of staff and form part of both Donor Partnership and Impact’s respective management teams. They will engage with multiple departments and colleagues across EBRD, with frequent external outreach and stakeholder engagement in the broader donor community and with actors on the international donor scene and regular interaction with users of donor finance within the Bank across all its key sector groups and policy teams. Equally, there will be engagement with the Bank’s shareholders on donor-related topics and various corporate teams including Risk and Debt Mobilisation.
**Background**
The Impact and Partnerships department supports the Bank’s operational and strategic objectives by mobilising and managing grants and concessional finance, maintaining relations with the Bank’s donor community and developing strategic partnerships. It also oversees the administration and approval of donor-funded activities, manages dedicated funds, and supports the Bank’s engagement with relevant external stakeholders.
The Donor Partnerships team leads on mobilising and managing donor funds in support of the Bank’s activities and on maintaining strategic relationships with EBRD’s bilateral and multilateral donor community. It develops and manages donor funding vehicles including the Shareholder Special Fund, supports fundraising and donor engagement, develops strategies and provides analysis, reporting, training and guidance to ensure strategic engagement with donors and effective use of donor resources across the Bank.
The Impact team leads on defining, measuring and communicating the Bank’s transition and development impact. Its responsibilities include the Bank’s transition results architecture and monitoring, assessment of the Bank’s contribution to broader development objectives, and the self-evaluation function. Within these responsibilities, the team assesses the use of concessional finance in EBRD projects and the impact of transactions with a blended finance component.
The Blended Finance Team, jointly positioned across Donor Partnerships and Impact, brings together the Bank’s donor and impact expertise to support the strategic and effective use of grants and blended finance. The Team leads the Bank’s donor and blended finance strategy and donor-facing policies, ensuring alignment between the Bank’s financing needs, donor priorities and the Bank’s transition and development objectives. It oversees compliance of blended finance operations with the Bank’s policies, guidelines and agreed DFI principles, including the principles governing the appropriate use of concessional finance and the avoidance of market distortion, as well as compliance with the Bank’s donor-focused policies.
The Team also provides strategic and technical advice to banking teams and fund managers on the design and use of blended finance, with a focus on ensuring that donor support maximises the impact and mobilisation potential of EBRD investments. It leads analysis and develops data and evidence on grants and blended finance, including its role in addressing market failures, generating additionality and impact, and mobilising finance. The Team is at the forefront of thought leadership on blended finance, engaging with donors, international development finance institutions and senior management, and representing EBRD in relevant international fora and discussions.
**Facts / Scale**
The Associate Director leads the work of the Blended Finance Team, bringing together the Bank’s donor partnerships and impact expertise to ensure that blended and concessional finance is strategically targeted, compliant with agreed principles and effective in delivering impact and mobilisation. Key responsibilities include:
* Custodian of donor related policies like the Donor Fee policy, Client Contribution Policy and related guidelines.
* Production of analysis and data for the annual Strategic Implementation Plan, regular Board reports, the annual Funding Outlook, scenario analysis, a new prioritisation system and other tools and reports
* Contributions to 7-10 country strategies and country snapshots annually, donor Knowledge Management products and think pieces, multiple internal and external requests for ad-hoc analysis
* Contributions to various reports including but not limited to an annual DFI Blended Finance Report, the EBRD Impact Report, Sustainability Report and Annual Report, and various donor reports. Production of the Annual Donor Report
* Organisation of at least 10 information and training session per year plus the Annual Donor Meeting
* Co-manage with Finance the annual donor fee budget including preparation of related policy and guidelines
* Supervision and quality control of analysis conducted by the team on the compliance of Bank’s investments with the internal guidelines for the deployment of blended and concessional finance (approx. 300 projects per year);
* Coordination of the Blended finance team advisory function
* Contribution to impact deep dives and thought pieces on the economics of blended finance
* Management of a team of 8-9 staff with links into both Donor Partnerships and Impact
**Accountabilities & Responsibilities**
Working under the guidance of the Director Donor Partnerships and the Director Impact, the Associate Director will:
* Promote an effective and impactful EBRD policy framework and a clear strategy for working with donors based on best international practice, reflecting key trends in the global development agenda and fully aligned with the Bank’s five year Strategic and Capital Framework (SCF) and key policies. This involves leading the design of donor-related policies and overseeing their implementation plus developing related guidelines and processes as well as monitoring the implementation of the 2026-2030 Donor Strategy;
* Ensure the quality, consistency and compliance of the Bank’s blended finance activities. The post holder will oversee the Team’s assessment of proposed and existing uses of concessional finance, ensuring compliance with the Bank’s guidelines and agreed DFI Principles for Blended Finance, including principles relating to market failure, additionality, impact and avoidance of market distortion. This includes providing quality control and strategic oversight of assessments undertaken by team members and ensuring consistent application of the framework across sectors and operations. The post holder will also develop and contribute to sharing relevant information on blended finance concessionality at project level for relevant audiences
* Lead the Blended Finance/Advisory function. The post holder will offer support to banking colleagues in the design of effective blended finance structures working across teams, in line with the DFI Principles for Blended Finance. They will also advice colleagues engaged in fundraising on best practice blended finance options and optimal structures for maximising impact, address bankability constraints, mobilising donor support plus private capital and provide relevant analysis.
* Lead the development of data, analysis and evidence on donor and blended finance, ensuring that the Bank has timely and high-quality information to support strategy, policy, operational decision-making and external engagement. This includes analysis of the use and impact of donor resources, the effectiveness of concessional finance, market failures, additionality, mobilisation and broader global trends in development and blended finance. The post holder will oversee the development of appropriate systems, tools and metrics and ensure high-quality inputs to corporate reporting, including the Annual Donor Report, Impact Report and other strategic and donor-specific reporting;
* Represent the Bank in international donor fora like the OECD, UN events on SDGs and Aid Effectiveness, GIIN, Convergence and IFI working groups on blended finance. Represent the Bank and engage with key stakeholders and peers in various international working groups on broader donor and development-related topics and blended finance debates making sure EBRD’s views and experience is effectively represented and emerging IFI best practice and joint policies are compatible with EBRD’s business model;
* Contribute to the strategic usage of donor resources and planning of fundraising efforts, to ensure it is an integral part of the Bank’s business and strategic direction and meets its need for external support. This will involve, on the one hand, mapping the Bank’s needs for donor support and availability of resources and, on the other, establishing effective tools and processes for matching supply and demand of donor resources, working in close collaboration with Banking and Policy teams using such resources and Donor Partnerships colleagues managing donor funds and relations. Such needs shall be incorporated in the corporate planning processes and strategic implementation plans, country and sector strategies and relevant policies;
* Promote awareness and information on the Bank’s donor agenda and use of concessional finance through organisation of information-sharing events including the Donor Network, topical events with external stakeholders, engagement with the Board of the Bank and the Bank’s Annual Donor Meeting. Develop and organise a training programme for staff on blended finance and various donor related aspects;
* Lead and manage the Blended Finance Hub, setting its strategic direction, priorities and work programme and ensuring effective integration of its Donor Partnerships and Impact responsibilities. This includes recruitment, goal setting, performance management, motivating, coaching and staff development, as well as ensuring effective collaboration with the wider Impact and Partnerships department and relevant Bank-wide teams.
* Champion and role model the Bank’s Behavioural Competencies and Corporate Behaviours, ensuring adherence within the team(s) so that the highest standards of integrity and ethical conduct are exhibited at all times.
**Knowledge, Skills, Experience & Qualifications**
**Experience**
* Extensive work experience and knowledge of working with donors and international development cooperation, in both a bilateral and multilateral context including in a strategy, policy or donor fund management role;
* Extensive experience in international development finance and blended finance design, mobilisation and resource management. Experience with project finance and financial structuring of projects to fit the mandate of a private investment facing International Development Financial Institution would be an advantage.
* Extensive experience in working on impact and additionality assessment of blended finance operations;
* Experience working for / with Development Financial Institutions/Multilateral Development Banks;
* Strong leadership skills. Proven successful experience in leading and managing people and guiding and motivating teams;
**Knowledge**
* Deep understanding of the global development agenda including UN, EU G7 and G20 priorities, emerging donor policy priorities, challenges facing the global aid architecture and best practice for use of donor funds;
* Deep understanding of the international blended finance and private capital mobilisation debates, key actors, emerging policies and trends, and various effective blended finance structures;
* Deep understanding of the international blended finance and private capital mobilisation debates, key actors, emerging policies and trends, and various effective blended finance structures;
* Deep understanding of the economics of blended finance, and of the principles guiding DFIs in the use of concessional funding;
* Strong understanding of approaches to mobilising support from donors and development finance partners across a range of concessional instruments (grants, concessional loans, guarantees, risk-sharing, equity, etc.) and governance, policies and approaches for high impact and efficient use of such donor support including the importance of sound financial and results management;

**Skills**

Some of the world's largest exchanges, banks and government agencies rely on our screening, monitoring and investigation products, and the industry they serve is at an inflection point. Compliance teams everywhere are looking to AI to make their work dramatically more efficient, freeing their people to focus on the judgement calls that genuinely need a human, with every automated decision auditable and explainable. Elliptic is building that future with our customers, not just for them, and this role owns it.
You will lead the product managers responsible for our core compliance portfolio, spanning wallet and transaction screening, continuous monitoring, on-chain investigations and risk configuration, and you will drive the product side of our agentic compliance programme alongside our design partners. Much of what you build will have no precedent. You will be inventing the category, inside the company with the data, intelligence and customer trust to win it.
This is a player-coach role reporting to the VP of Product. You will lead and grow a team of product managers and personally own some of the hardest problems on the roadmap. The product organisation is centred in London with a growing US presence.
## What you'll do
* **Own the vision, strategy and roadmap** for Elliptic's compliance portfolio, and define what these products become as AI reshapes how compliance work gets done.
* **Lead product for our agentic compliance programme**: AI capabilities that make compliance work faster and better, with auditability and explainability designed in from the start.
* **Lead, coach and grow a team of product managers.** Hire well, develop people deliberately, and set the standard for how a modern, AI-augmented PM works. Developing product talent is a core output of this role, not a side effect.
* **Stay obsessively close to customers, in creative ways**: Methods such as design partnerships, analyst shadowing, product instrumentation, and internal dogfooding before anything ships come naturally to you to increase the chances of success. Convert ambiguous market signal into a clear view of what to build and why.
* **Prioritise ruthlessly.** Demand will always exceed capacity. Sequence zero-to-one bets against the needs of products customers depend on today, and say yes or no credibly, with reasoning people can engage with.
* **Execute with rigour, raising velocity and quality together.** Own outcomes, not shipping dates. Use AI across your own workflow and your team's to learn faster and ship better at the same time, in a domain where mistakes carry real consequences.
## What this role is not
* **Not a compliance officer role.** You are building the products compliance teams use, not running a compliance programme.
* **Not a caretaker role.** The core products are successful and deeply embedded; the mandate is reinvention.
* **Not a management-only layer.** You will lead product managers and personally do product work on the hardest problems.
## Who we're looking for
* **10+ years building software products**, including leading and developing product managers, with people who are better because they worked with you.
* **A genuine zero-to-one track record**: an ambiguous problem in a complex domain, taken from nothing to a product real users depend on.

* **High self-sufficiency**: you find high-value opportunities no one assigned you, create clarity rather than wait for it, and are comfortable owning a broad remit while the map is still being drawn.
* **Continuous systems thinking**: you look for the repeatable system behind every one-off fix, building leverage so each problem solved makes the whole team permanently faster.
* **A data-informed operating style**: you instrument what you ship, argue from evidence, and change your mind when the data disagrees.
* **Judgement under ambiguity**: you know which decisions to make fast and which to hold open when precedent does not exist.
* **Comfort in regulated, high-stakes environments**: you treat trust, explainability and defensibility as features, and operate well at the tension point between innovation and regulatory reality.
* **Restlessness about velocity and quality**: you treat "that's just how long it takes" as a claim to be tested.

Own design across your domain
Be accountable for the quality of design across the pods in your domain.
Work autonomously on complex and ambiguous problems, bringing structure and design thinking when the path isn’t obvious.
Identify opportunities and bring ideas to the team rather than waiting for a brief.
Understand the wider customer journey and how your work fits into the experience beyond your immediate feature or pod.
Understand that the job doesn’t end with delivery. You will monitor, understand and find new opportunities once initiatives have gone live.
Use discovery to reduce risk
Decide what level of discovery an initiative needs based on its size, risk and uncertainty.
Choose the right research or testing approach for the question you’re trying to answer.
Work with the research team to recruit, test, synthesise and communicate evidence where appropriate.
Clearly separate what we learn from what we’re assuming.
Challenge when important decisions are being made without enough evidence, and make the risk visible.
Bring customer evidence into product decisions rather than treating research as a separate phase of the process.

Understand the commercial context of your domain, the KPIs your work can influence and the constraints we operate within.
Identify and navigate customer, business, technical and regulatory trade-offs, challenging requirements when there’s a good reason to do so.
Partner with your PM on roadmap thinking, sequencing and product decisions.

Create thoughtful, robust experiences that work beyond the happy path, including real data, states, permissions, edge cases and errors.
Use our design system fluently, extending it deliberately where needed, while working with other designers to maintain consistency across domains.
Build accessibility into your work from the start and use principles, evidence and constraints to explain your design decisions.
Get things shipped
Take work from early exploration through to build, launch and beyond, staying close to the outcome.
Plan and sequence design work so Engineering isn’t held up by missing decisions or designs.
Manage competing priorities across multiple pods, adapting to change without losing sight of the customer problem or design quality.
Influence through collaboration
Be customer obsessed and a strong voice for the customer in your domain, grounded in evidence.
Work closely with Product and Engineering from the beginning, making key decisions together as a pod rather than as individual disciplines.
Communicate clearly with everyone from your immediate pod to senior stakeholders, balancing customer needs with commercial and technical constraints.
Help other designers grow
Share your thinking, approaches and lessons with the wider design team.
Raise the quality of the work around you through critique, collaboration and example.
Contribute to making design at Equals a place where people can do their best work.
Use AI and new tools to work differently
Use AI and prototyping tools to explore ideas, test concepts and answer questions quickly.
Use AI to reduce the time spent on work that doesn’t require design judgement, creating more space for thinking, discovery and craft.
Build working prototypes when they can accelerate learning, within agreed technical boundaries and in partnership with Engineering.

A strong understanding of interaction design, information architecture and visual design.
Experience conducting or working closely with user research and usability testing.
Experience working with and contributing to a design system.
A high bar for accessibility, interaction quality and the details that make products work well.
The ability to communicate and defend design decisions clearly, while being open to changing your mind.
Experience mentoring or supporting other designers.
Experience using AI and emerging tools to work differently, accelerate design and prototyping, and spend more time on the work that requires design judgement.

After your first year, we’d expect you to be someone that your domain’s product and engineering teams rely on.

Act in and fulfill the role of the Data Protection Officer for our international entities.

Conduct regular Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs) or Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) to identify and mitigate potential privacy risks associated with new or existing projects.
Ensure that data subject requests such as data access, correction or deletion for individuals whose data is processed (EU and UK: employees, customers etc.), are managed and responded to within the required timeframe.
Oversee and advise on the implementation of data classification, data mapping and flows, privacy and protection and data retention controls and procedures.
Oversee and advise on incident response efforts in the event of a data breach, including coordination with internal and external stakeholders, timely notification, and remediation.
Monitor controls associated with the management, retention and disposal of records are maintained.

Collaborate with legal, IT, and other departments to ensure that data privacy considerations are embedded in data processing activities, system design, AI initiatives, and data handling procedures.
Provide guidance and training to employees on data protection regulations and best practices to enhance overall awareness and compliance.
Establish and maintain records of data processing activities, including data inventories, data flows, and data retention schedules.

5+ years of experience in data privacy and protection, with a strong understanding of relevant regulations and industry standards.
Experience acting as the Data Protection Officer and interfacing with data protection authorities.
Knowledge of U.S. and international data protection laws and regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) and their implications on data handling practices.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey complex data privacy concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a keen attention to detail.
Experience conducting privacy impact assessments and managing data subject requests.
Ability to work independently, manage multiple projects, and collaborate effectively across teams.
Demonstrated commitment to staying current with developments in data privacy and protection.

**About us**
The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.
At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

*Build a newsworthy career at the FT.*
**The role**
The Financial Times has an opening for a professional services correspondent to join the London Newsroom.
This is a new role designed to expand and elevate our coverage of the professional services sector as the world’s top corporate advisers respond to AI disruption, slower growth and intensifying scrutiny on their activities.
Professional services is a core part of the FT’s global corporate coverage and this reporter will be expected to break news on the big strategy and IT consultancies, particularly McKinsey, Boston Consulting Group, Bain and Accenture, as well as contributing to covering the advisory operations of the Big Four – Deloitte, EY, KPMG and PwC. Working closely with our other professional services reporters, in London and New York, the correspondent will chart how AI is reshaping the sector globally. The technology threatens to wipe out parts of consultants’ businesses and kill off their traditional hourly billing model. But executives argue that the upheaval also presents a massive opportunity for the sector as companies seek advice on how to overhaul their IT, workforces and strategies. There is scope to break stories about job cuts and changes to the sector’s staffing model as firms respond to sluggish demand and turn to AI to do tasks previously carried out by armies of junior consultants. The role will involve working with the FT’s global network to dig into how AI is disrupting IT consulting firms’ lucrative business implementing enterprise software products from the likes of SAP and Salesforce. The reporter must be able to deliver scoops and inside-the-room insight on the executives who run the big consultancies, their pay and C-suite power dynamics within the firms. The professional services sector has long been a source of regulatory and reputational scandals, while the incursion of private equity has fuelled the growth of challengers to the dominant players, offering great scope for original reporting that can attract readers to the FT. You will have to work closely with colleagues from across the newsroom, particularly the US Professional Services Editor and the London-based Accountancy Correspondent. You will also be expected to contribute across different media as the FT expands its professional services coverage. **Key responsibilities**
* Bring in high-profile scoops about the big professional services firms on issues such as: work won and lost, financial performance, strategic changes, adoption of AI and technology, behaviour and workplace culture, regulatory interventions, leadership changes and M&A.
* Deliver deeply reported analyses on the changing business models of professional services groups, their business relationships with AI, tech and software groups and their importance in wider society.
* Be the first to report on the roles of consultants in big corporate stories in other sectors, such as turnaround plans and strategic overhauls at blue-chip companies.
* Weekend shifts are required as part of the newsroom rota.
* Working with, and providing cover for, reporters on the professional services team during absences.
**Please submit your application by the end of the day, Monday 12th October 2026.**
**The use of AI**
Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations. We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.
**Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion**
We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.
FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

**Reliability, observability and operational correctness**
The priority is not simply whether the platform is up, but whether it is doing its job: client feeds arrive completely, surveillance runs against the right window and expected alerts fire.
You and the team will establish patterns for correctness monitoring, escalation, incident response and disaster recovery, allowing product teams to define their own alerts, service levels and response playbooks **Software craftsmanship and change safety**Alongside correctness, change safety is our other top engineering priority: the ability to change the platform frequently, in small increments, with confidence that nothing has quietly broken. That means tests that earn trust, reviews that catch design problems rather than typos, deployment that is boring, and the discipline to keep it that way under pressure. You will own the standard of engineering craft across Surveillance: what good looks like, how it is taught, and whether it holds when nobody is watching. **Architectural coherence**
Each team will make sensible local decisions. Your job is to make sure they add up: that we are not solving the same problem three ways, that the interfaces between domains are deliberate, and that the estate can still be reasoned about in two years.
You will set the technical direction others plan against, including how client environments are managed across their lifecycle and how software reaches production. **Security architecture**
Not governance, which sits with our Security team, but the engineering picture: how client environment isolation actually works, where the boundaries are, how privileged access is granted and removed, and which risks we have consciously accepted. This includes workload identity, SCIM 2.0 and enterprise identity integration for client provisioning.
Individual teams will secure their own patch. Somebody has to own how it fits together. Security policy, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification, the security risk register and the compliance programme are owned by our Security team. You own the engineering controls and technical evidence they depend on, working closely with Security rather than running a compliance function, and without becoming an approval gate. **Growing our senior engineers**
A Principal here is measured partly by the engineers around them. That means growing their scope rather than directing their work: helping them take on problems larger than a single team, raising the standard of design review and technical writing, and building a bench that does not route through you. **Cost and unit economics**
Cloud cost grows as we add new clients, so it needs to be an engineering concern.
You will work with the teams building our products and our FinOps engineering effort to improve optimisation, capacity strategy and client-level cost visibility. Cost is a shared responsibility, not something owned in isolation. **Enterprise client assurance and commercial support**

You will also review deals for technical risk and represent our architecture with client CISOs and technical stakeholders. **What success looks like**
The technical direction is already established. You will inherit goals in flight and formulate plans to deliver the desired outcomes.
We want someone who can get close to the full technology environment and team quickly, build on what is working and move at pace rather than returning to first principles.
Success means teams can move safely and faster because of the platform and the standards, with less operational toil and a growing proportion of engineering time spent on elective work rather than keeping the lights on.
That means:
* Client onboarding becomes increasingly automated end to end.
* Observability lets teams answer common operational questions without elevated production access.
* Change is frequent, small and reversible, and incidents do not scale with deployment frequency.

# ******Job Description Summary******
The Europe & Asia Transportation Planning & Execution Manager is responsible for translating global transportation strategy into executable regional transportation plans across Europe and Asia. This role develops routing plans, execution models, localized processes, and supplier-management routines that enable consistent, scalable transportation performance across sites, suppliers, carriers, and lanes. 1. A key priority for this role is to plan the week and monitor the day to deliver CTL and CTB weekly objectives. The successful candidate will leverage AI, analytics, digital tools, and process automation to improve transportation quality, strengthen execution discipline, accelerate continuous improvement, and deliver measurable cost and productivity benefits. These additions align with the draft’s stated focus on performance management, continuous improvement, and turning strategy into repeatable execution capability This is not primarily a shipment-tracking or expediting role. It operates one level above individual shipment execution and is accountable for building the routing, processes, supplier routines, and operating mechanisms that enable reliable transportation performance at scale.
# **Job Description**
## **Essential Responsibilities**
* Develop and maintain transportation routing plans for Europe and Asia aligned with global transportation strategy, including mode selection, carrier assignments, gateway strategy, consolidation approach, cutoff requirements, transit-time expectations, contingency routing, and escalation requirements.
* Translate transportation strategy into executable lane, site, supplier, system, and process-level plans that can be consistently deployed across the region.
* Establish implementation plans for major transportation changes, including supplier readiness, site readiness, carrier onboarding, routing instructions, systems requirements, data requirements, communications, escalation paths, and performance monitoring.
* Translate global transportation standard work into practical regional processes while allowing appropriate localization for infrastructure, supplier capability, operating hours, regulatory requirements, and market conditions.
* Standardize successful processes across sites and suppliers and reduce unnecessary regional variation caused by legacy local practices.
* Serve as a primary regional interface with transportation suppliers across Europe and Asia, including freight forwarders, airlines, trucking providers, parcel/express carriers, and 4PL partners.
* Ensure suppliers understand and execute routing, service, data, escalation, and performance requirements; conduct operating reviews and drive corrective action when performance does not meet expectations.
* Lead implementation of transportation plans across GE Aerospace sites and suppliers throughout Europe and Asia, ensuring clarity on provider selection, shipment timing, routing, documentation, cutoffs, escalation procedures, data requirements, and compliance expectations.
* Support supplier launches, sourcing transitions, manufacturing transfers, new facilities, MRO expansions, distribution-network changes, and other major supply-chain initiatives.
* Lead the regional operating rhythm by **planning the week and monitoring the day** to deliver **CTL and CTB weekly objectives**, using daily visibility and exception management to identify gaps early and drive countermeasures.
* Monitor performance across transit time, routing compliance, carrier performance, lane reliability, premium freight, shipment exceptions, lead-time performance, supplier execution, data quality, capacity constraints, and recurring failure modes.
* Use **AI, analytics, digital tools, and automation** to improve decision making, transportation visibility, process discipline, data quality, continuous improvement, and cost performance.
* Identify and scale technology-enabled opportunities to reduce waste, improve quality, lower premium freight, and deliver measurable cost and productivity benefits.
* Drive structured problem solving and continuous improvement with sites, suppliers, carriers, and transportation partners.
* Partner closely with regional distribution capabilities, including Netherlands and Singapore spare-parts operations, to ensure integration into the global transportation network.

Colibrium Additive is seeking a Global Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Leader to establish, scale, and continuously improve a risk-based EHS program across our global operations. This leader will set the strategic direction for EHS, build a strong culture of care and accountability, and use data, technology, and cross-functional partnership to keep our people safe and our operations compliant, resilient, and future-ready. The role suits a strategic and hands-on leader with deep EHS expertise, strong influencing skills, and a track record of driving measurable improvement in complex, multi-site industrial environments — including those with additive manufacturing and metal powder hazards.
# **Job Description**
**Key Responsibilities**
**Strategy & Governance**
Develop, implement, and sustain a global EHS strategy, policies, and standards aligned with business priorities and regulatory requirements.
Establish governance mechanisms to ensure consistent EHS expectations, accountability, and execution across all sites.
**Risk Management & Operational Excellence**
Lead enterprise and site-level risk assessments, EHS audits, and management system reviews; prioritize corrective and preventive actions to reduce risk.
Implement sustainable controls for key hazards relevant to the business, including high-risk operations such as metal powder/process safety.

**Culture, Leadership & Capability Building**

Provide clear reporting for leadership reviews, including progress versus goals, systemic risks, and improvement roadmap status.
**Incident Management & Learning**
Lead incident investigations and root cause analyses; ensure timely, transparent closure and verification of corrective actions.
Drive organizational learning by sharing insights, improving leading indicators, and focusing on prevention-oriented actions.
**Cross-Functional Partnership & External Awareness**
Partner with Production, Engineering, Service, HR, and Legal to embed EHS and ergonomics considerations into core business processes, change management, facility planning, and investment decisions.
Maintain awareness of regulatory changes, emerging risks (including those tied to new materials, automation, and additive manufacturing processes), and industry best practices, keeping the business compliant and proactive.
Build and maintain an active network with EHS colleagues across GE Aerospace and the broader industry to share best practices and accelerate adoption of proven approaches.

* Language: Business fluency in English required; German and/or French is a plus given the site footprint.
* Travel: Ability and willingness to travel approximately 30%, with flexibility for more during peak project periods.
**Preferred Qualifications / Desired Characteristics**
* Certifications: CSP, CIH, NEBOSH, or equivalent professional EHS certification strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated success building and scaling EHS programs across complex operations and driving measurable improvement in safety outcomes.
* Domain expertise in high-hazard operations, including additive manufacturing environments, metal powder hazards, and process safety management.
* Comfort using EHS data platforms, dashboards, and digital tools to drive decisions and reporting.
* Strong influencing, communication, and stakeholder management skills across all organizational levels, from the shop floor to senior leadership.
