| **About Nscale** |
Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.
We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you’ll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you’ll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.
| |
| --- |
| **About the Role (Job Purpose)** |
Commissioning is the last gate between capital spent and capacity earning. On contracted AI campuses it is a contractual event with dates, evidence requirements and remedies attached — not an internal quality exercise.
As a Director of Commissioning you own that gate. You will set the single standard by which every megawatt Nscale builds is proven, hold the authority to accept or refuse capacity on the company’s behalf, and build a commissioning and operational readiness function that scales from a 20MW first phase to multi-gigawatt campuses without the standard slipping as volume rises.
This is a build role. The function does not yet exist in its target form — the standard, the tooling, the team and the operating model are all to be created. Our portfolio spans Norway, the UK, Finland and the United States, and the technical scope is harder than conventional colocation: closed-loop direct-to-chip liquid cooling at high rack densities, Arctic and extreme-ambient operation, high-voltage grid interfaces, on-site generation and storage, and heat-reuse obligations.
| |
| --- |
| **What You’ll be Doing (Responsibilities)** |
* Author and own the Group Commissioning Execution Standard — the L0–L6 framework, test scripts, witness and evidence rules, defect taxonomy and turnover package specification — and make sure it is applied, not just published.
* Hold the acceptance gate: no system is energised, accepted or handed over anywhere in the group without your sign-off, and you hold that position under schedule and commercial pressure.
* Select, deploy and govern a single commissioning management platform so evidence, defects and progress are visible in one place across the portfolio.
* Make sure commissioning is built into every project master programme from the outset, and give early, evidence-based warning when energisation or acceptance dates are at risk.
* Work with Procurement, Legal and Delivery so acceptance criteria, witness rights, test obligations and turnover standards are written into EPC and OEM packages before they are let.
* Own the methodology for closed-loop direct-to-chip liquid cooling — CDU factory testing, secondary-loop flushing and passivation, water chemistry, per-rack flow balancing, leak detection, failover under thermal transient.
* Own high-consequence electrical testing: HV energisation sequencing with network operators, protection coordination and primary injection, black-building and utility-failure testing at full simulated load.
* Recruit, develop and retain a scarce, internationally mobile discipline — including in locations where the local specialist market is thin — and build succession so no hall depends on one individual.
* Own operational readiness and the transfer to Operations: complete as-builts and O&M, populated CMMS, spares on site, tested SOPs, EOPs and MOPs, and operations staff assessed as competent before capacity is accepted.
* Set the safe-systems-of-work regime for energisation and testing across every jurisdiction we operate in, and satisfy each local regulatory and inspection regime without running three parallel ways of working.
* Lead the commissioning relationship with tenants and their acceptance teams, and support lenders, insurers and certification bodies where commissioning evidence is a diligence item.
| |
| --- |
| **About You (Skills / Qualifications)** |
* A substantial career in critical facilities engineering — indicatively 15+ years — including 8+ years leading commissioning at programme or portfolio level rather than on a single project.
* Owner-side or client-side accountability for accepting large-scale data centre capacity. Contractor-side commissioning leadership alone will not be enough; this role has to hold a gate against the party delivering the work.
* Personally led integrated systems testing (L5) through to acceptance on at least two hyperscale or AI data centre projects of 50MW or greater.
* Direct experience of high-density liquid-cooled deployments — direct-to-chip, CDUs, secondary loops, water chemistry — or closely adjacent depth and clear evidence of learning an unfamiliar technology quickly and rigorously.
* High-voltage and medium-voltage commissioning experience, including energisation sequencing with network operators and protection coordination.
* Built and led multi-disciplinary technical teams across borders, time zones and languages.
* Contract literacy: EPC contracting forms, acceptance and handover mechanisms, witness rights, warranty provisions and the evidentiary basis of claims.
* Experience across more than one regulatory jurisdiction, and the judgement to build one standard that satisfies several regimes rather than three parallel ones.
* A degree in electrical or mechanical engineering, or equivalent demonstrable expertise.
* Credible at both ends of the organisation — able to hold a technical argument with a lead commissioning engineer on site in the morning and present acceptance risk to the Executive in the afternoon.
* Willing and able to travel internationally at **60–70%, including to remote Arctic sites in winter conditions.**
* Right to work in the UK or Norway, or eligibility for sponsorship.
**Nice to Have**
* Nordic market experience and familiarity with NEK 400, FSE and the DSB regime; Norwegian or another Scandinavian language.
* Tenant acceptance testing with a major hyperscale counterparty.
* Exposure to Uptime Institute certification, lenders’ technical adviser processes or insurer-driven assurance regimes.
* Hands-on use of commissioning management platforms and Primavera P6.
* BESS, on-site generation or heat-reuse offtake commissioning.
* Chartered or professionally registered engineer (CEng, PE or equivalent).
* Experience in a rapidly scaling business, where the standard has to be built while the programme is already running.
**Why this role matters**
**A function to build.** The standard, the tooling, the team and the operating model are all yours to create. You will define how Nscale proves every megawatt it builds for the next decade.
**Scale and a genuine technical frontier.** A multi-gigawatt pipeline across four countries, built around liquid-cooled AI infrastructure at densities that make integrated testing meaningfully harder than conventional data centre work — and more interesting.
| |
| --- |
| **What We Can Offer You** |
You’ll have the opportunity to help shape the operating standards behind a next-generation AI cloud platform, working on complex infrastructure challenges with real ownership and impact. This is a chance to play a meaningful role in scaling high-performance, sustainable data centre operations in a fast-moving environment.
Relocation support is available. Given lead times in this discipline, candidates with extended notice periods will still be considered, though earliest availability is an advantage.

Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.

Why we're hiring
We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled builders like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software.
This is a product role, and your product is how Odin operates. Think of it as our ghostbuster: every operational problem lands with you, you decide what gets fixed, and you ship most of the fixes yourself rather than writing tickets for someone else.
We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.
Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we'll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.
The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.
We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.
Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it.
The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too.
We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.
What you'll own
Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself.
Cost per deal: There will be big early wins where a whole process can be ripped out and replaced. After that, doubling ops efficiency comes from 150 small changes, and you'll be the one making them.
Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached.
Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it.
The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them.
What we're looking for
You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar.
Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start.
Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it.
A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.
In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.
Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.
Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV.
How we work
There are five things we care about deeply:
Reason from the ground up
Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.
Speed begets speed
We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.
Take ownership
Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.
Brutal honesty
If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.
Truly excellent customer service
Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

You prefer close management of your responsibilities;
You are risk-averse;

You take yourself too seriously;
You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact

# Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
London
## Our Mission
At Ophelos, we believe in a different way to deal with debt. One that puts empathy and understanding front and centre, approaching our customers as individuals — no matter what they’re going through.
For too long, people in debt have borne the brunt of poor industry practices. Intimidating tactics, time-consuming customer service and a one-size-fits-all approach that overlooks the reasons *anyone* can fall into debt in the first place. Meanwhile, businesses suffer too. Poor customer experience translates to poor customer satisfaction, high churn rates, bad brand reputation and ultimately missed opportunities.
That’s why we’re taking a radically different approach. Pioneering an industry-first AI-native collections platform, we build products that help individuals clear their debts in a way that suits them, whilst providing businesses with an improved customer experience and game-changing insights into their customer base.
Since our launch in 2021, we’ve worked with some of the UK’s leading companies, including Octopus, Scottish Power and Philips — helping millions of people move toward a more stable, debt-free future. In 2023, we were acquired by Intrum, Europe’s biggest credit management service and have begun the next phase in our growth — expansion into 17 European markets over the next two years.
# **About Ophelos**
At Ophelos, we are reimagining credit, collections, and financial health infrastructure across Europe. Our mission is to build fairer, smarter, and more empathetic financial systems through modern software engineering, data science, and thoughtful product design.
As we expand into new markets across Europe, we face a core challenge: adapting to complex local banking standards, regulatory requirements, payment systems, and client integrations while maintaining a clean, scalable core platform. That’s where Forward Deployed Engineering comes in.
# **The Role**
Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) make Ophelos work in each market without changing what Ophelos fundamentally is. FDEs operate right at the intersection of high-calibre software engineering and real-world market expansion.
In this role, you will hold a unique position across Engineering and Markets:
* **Engineering owns your growth & craft:** You are held to rigorous engineering standards—code reviews, architecture design, technical excellence, line management, progression, and pay.
* **Markets owns the priorities:** You work hand-in-hand with named Markets counterparts to prioritize client deployments, integrations, and go-live schedules.
# **What You'll Do**
* **Edge & Integration Engineering:** Build, scale, and optimize per-market client data ingestion and egestion integrations, including APIs, file formats, validation, reconciliation, and replay mechanisms.
* **Payment & Comms Integration:** Connect market-specific payment providers, SMS, email, postal, and messaging vendor APIs through clean platform abstractions.
* **Configuration & Localisation:** Leverage and expand existing configuration surfaces to adapt Ophelos to local regulations and workflow needs.
* **Market Operations & Defects:** Own and resolve market-specific defects within the integration and configuration layers.
* **Field-to-Roadmap Influence:** Collect market needs, measure commercial impact, and author structured Product Cases stating unlock value to shape the core product roadmap.
* **Client & Partner Engagement:** Partner directly with Markets Success and client technical teams during onboarding across Europe.
# **Our Operating Principles**
We solve complex market expansion through structured decision-making:
1. **Configure First:** Solve requests using existing product configuration surfaces to deliver fast, maintainable solutions.
2. **Integrate at the Edge:** Build robust integration layers against clean, stable Abstraction APIs.
3. **Escalate with Impact:** When core capabilities are missing, build compelling business cases to drive product platform development rather than modifying core code directly.
## **Role Expectations & Responsibilities**
* Owns complete market onboarding end-to-end, acting as the primary technical authority in client discussions.
* Aggregates multi-market needs into the Abstraction API roadmap with product engineering.
* Builds reusable integration patterns, market playbooks, and mentors mid-level FDEs.
* Confidently leads technical and executive-level discussions with enterprise financial institutions.
# **What We’re Looking For**
## **Core Technical Requirements**
* **Strong Software Engineering Skills:** Production proficiency in Python and TypeScript, with Ruby experience considered a plus.
* **Data Fluency Under Failure:** Hands-on experience with complex schemas, data transformation, validation, reconciliation, idempotency, and replay logic.
* **Third-Party Integration Experience:** Demonstrated ability to evaluate, map, and integrate third-party APIs and protocols safely and reliably.
* **Cross-Functional Communication:** Ability to translate technical details clearly to client executives, product managers, and software engineers alike.
* **Documentation & AI-First Mindset:** Habitual documentation practices and comfort working in an AI-first development environment using tools like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenSpec.
* **Location & Travel:** Willingness to work 3 days a week from our London office in Liverpool Street and travel periodically across Europe.
## **Senior Experience & Domain Expertise**
* **Regulated Domain Experience:** Background in collections, credit, payments, fintech, or adjacent regulated sectors.
* **Enterprise Onboarding:** Track record of navigating complex client data models and multi-stakeholder corporate integrations.
* **Roadmap Influence:** Demonstrated experience building business cases that successfully influenced core product roadmaps.
# **Why Join Us?**
* **High Impact:** Directly shape how Ophelos scales into new European markets.
* **Technical Rigour:** Work with high engineering standards without sacrificing market agility.
* **Career Growth:** Clear progression framework within a rapidly expanding company.
* **Modern Stack & Workflows:** AI-first engineering practices and modern tools.
Ophelos is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

* The ability to thrive in a green-field environment where you can build, test, and iterate quickly
* Comfort collaborating across international markets, working alongside local teams to ensure campaigns resonate

* Prototype in code where it beats Figma, submit your own PRs for small front end fixes, and QA what ships.
* Be the person Support, Sales and Legal come to when a check is stuck or a customer asks what a vendor does with their data. You'll know the domain better than almost anyone in the company within 90 days.

* Multi state workflows in the portfolio, such as orders, cases, applications and checks, where the system decides the next step and the design has to handle the moments when it can't

* Production ready UI craft that clears a high bar, shown in the portfolio
* Ownership of the call when the data isn't there: deciding, explaining the reasoning, owning the outcome, and solving the problem in front of you whether or not it is strictly a design problem. Over time, pulling the squad towards research backed judgement as the norm

* Bonus points for HR tech or ATS experience, and for credits, billing or usage based pricing

S106 and Monitoring Officer - Maldon District Council
Permanent, Full Time
£49,435.14 - £54,930.60 per annum
Location: Maldon
Closing Date: 26th October 2026
Maldon District Council is working in partnership with Essex Shared Services to support the recruitment of the role of a S106 and Monitoring Officer, a full-time position offering hybrid working with a minimum of 2 days in the office per week. Office attendance will be in line with the needs of the Council and the Planning Policy Team, including occasional evening committees or meetings where necessary. Check out Maldon's careers page to see what it's like to work for Maldon District Council.
The role is within the Council's Planning Policy team, which is part of the Place, Planning & Growth directorate. This is an exciting time to join the Planning Policy Team at Maldon District Council. The Council has recently agreed proposals to commence preparation of the new Local Plan. We are the first local authority in Essex to be producing a Local Plan under the new 30-month plan-making system, which will set out a long-term vision for Maldon District, including where homes, jobs and infrastructure should be located, how high-quality design will be supported and how the district's distinctive natural and historic environment will be protected and enhanced.
We are also involved in a wide range of ongoing planning policy work outside of the new Local Plan, including supporting Parish Councils with neighbourhood plans, managing S106 agreements, undertaking monitoring activities and producing the Authority Monitoring Report (AMR). Alongside this, we are also working closely with our Development Management colleagues on a number of significant development proposals currently being brought forward by developers.
As the Council's S106 and Monitoring Officer, you will support the Planning Policy Team to focus on delivery of the Local Plan by leading on the following key accountabilities:
* Maintain and manage accurate records of Section 106 agreements, unilateral undertakings and associated planning obligations, including financial contributions, affordable housing, open space, highways, education, health, biodiversity, environmental mitigation and other infrastructure requirements.
* Monitor the implementation of Section 106 obligations, including triggers, commencement dates, payment points, indexation, spend deadlines and delivery of non-financial obligations.

# Senior Backend Engineer (Data serving)
## Location

OverviewApplication
## **About Pleo**
Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.
The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.
Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.
**Please note: applications will be open until Tuesday 13th October 2026 at 08.00 CEST. We will not review any application before the closing date so please use this time to submit a high quality application.**
## **About the role**
We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the Data Serving team that owns the production-grade boundary between Pleo's raw product data and everyone who consumes it, including internal product teams, AI agents, and customers directly accessing their own data. This Senior Backend Engineer role builds and owns that boundary: APIs and the low-latency serving layer underneath it. You will build customer-facing infrastructure where contract stability and latency are non-negotiable, and where the clean abstraction you maintain is what lets every downstream consumer trust the data without ever touching a raw source.
## **Who you’ll be working with and reporting to**
You will report to our Senior Manager of Data & AI Products, and work closely with our Staff Data Platform Engineer, Data Engineers, Product Managers and others Engineers across the business. You'll also coordinate closely with the GenAI Platform and Data Infrastructure teams.
## **What you’ll be doing**
As a Senior Backend Engineer, you will:
* Build and own the Data API boundary: delivering clean, versioned, and performant endpoints for internal dashboards, customer-facing features, and third-party tools (e.g., Fivetran connectors via incremental syncs and cursor pagination).
* Design and optimise the read models, indexes, and caching strategies in Postgres (and future OLAP stores) to guarantee low-latency query performance.
* Build reliable integrations with Pleo’s Kotlin-based product backend services to ensure the serving layer surfaces the correct data required for a customer facing feature.
* Own the reliability and performance of the services you build: monitoring, incident response, and SLOs appropriate to customer-facing infrastructure.
* Partner with Data Engineers to define clean contracts between the ingestion/aggregation layer and the serving DB, ensuring read patterns match storage schemas.
* Partner with the Authorization team to secure APIs using industry-standard authentication and authorization protocols.
* Build a near-real-time data aggregation service to collect and unify data across Pleo services.
* Design metadata, lineage, and governance capabilities that make the serving layer explainable, auditable, and trustworthy.
* Own access control and permission management services, including row and column-level data access with full audit trails.
To put things into context, you can expect to work with the following tech stack: AWS (product side), GCP (data side), Docker, Kubernetes, BigQuery, PostgreSQL dbt, Kafka, Airflow, Python, Kotlin and more!
## **What you bring**
You’ll thrive in this role if you have:
* Strong backend engineering experience building and owning reporting and analytics API services and serving-layer infrastructure.
* A mindset focusing on reliability, latency, and SLOs.
* Experience owning API boundary layers including clean endpoint design, versioning, contract stability, and ensuring downstream consumers are never exposed to raw data sources.
* Strong expertise designing performant read-heavy systems, including relational database optimisation, indexing strategies, materialised views, caching, and API performance tuning.
* Solid database fundamentals (SQL and non-SQL) and strong SQL querying skills, as well as deep expertise in Kafka.
* Deep experience with a JVM-based language (Pleo's product backend is Kotlin-based).
* AWS or GCP with Kubernetes experience. You must be familiar with configuring, deploying and operating containerised applications in a k8s environment.
* Experience working at the boundary between data systems and product backend services, with a real understanding of the operational differences between the two.
* The ability to move quickly and independently. This is a hands-on delivery role with clear scope, not an architecture or advisory engagement.
* Experience in fintech, payments, or other regulated product environments.
## **Why is this role a good fit for you**
This role is a good fit for you if:
* You are passionate about building systems that serve other engineers.
* You understand what it means to design, build and maintain services with high performance, availability and reliability requirements.
* You have a very deep understanding of the data world and know how to bridge the gap between data and engineering.
This role is not a good fit for you if:
* You need to operate within very large and structured teams with clear hierarchy. This role sits within a small and specialist team with a lot of autonomy.
* You do not wish to be responsible for services with high availability requirements. You will be held accountable for the quality and availability of those services alongside your team.
* You prefer to be handed over clearly defined scope of work. You will be expected to define and design the solutions as much as building them.
## **How you’ll develop in this role**
In your first 6 months at Pleo, you will:
* Get deep into the current state: the upstream Kotlin services the serving layer will pull from, the internal consumers already waiting on the API (Data & AI Products, GenAI Platform), and any prototype serving logic that needs to be replaced or formalised.
* Ship the first production version of the Reporting API (a defined set of endpoints with agreed contracts, versioning, and SLOs) with at least one internal consumer live against it.
* Establish the access control, tenant isolation, and row/column-level security model for the API. You will have proven out low-latency query performance on Postgres, with clear metrics around reliability and SLOs, and established a clear architectural benchmark to understand when (or if) an OLAP layer would ever be necessary.
Please note: We can hire on a remote, hybrid or in-person set-up in any of the locations listed on the advert but you will need to be physically based in the country of your choice with a valid right to work. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any of the listed locations.
## **Show me the benefits**
* Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)
* Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office
* Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis.
* 25 days of annual leave + public holidays (additional days may apply in select countries based on local standards).
* For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options.
* We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far
* Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work
## **The interview process**
We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:
1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
2. Core skills test: An async AI-assisted programming test to assess your coding fundamentals.
3. Hiring Manager interview: A 60-minute chat deep diving into your experience.
4. Pleo Challenge: A 75-minute system design interview focusing on your architecture, infrastructure and problem-solving skills.
Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!
With this in mind, we want to help you understand what we really care about when reviewing your application:
* We receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI - it’s a big focus for us internally too- but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you - not AI - know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background.
* Every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.
* This role focuses heavily on building services for internal / external users consumption. It is absolutely critical to have extensive API design and development experience, expertise in OLAP systems and to be able to work in Kotlin. Ensure your CV reflects clearly of the actual experience you have across those areas.
## **About your application**
* **English first.** Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.
* **A fair look for everyone.** Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.
* **Diversity drives us.** We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.
* **Interview at your best.** We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.
* **Your data is safe.** When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.
* **Applying for multiple roles?** Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.
* **Reapplying.** If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

## Role Summary
Developer Success is the technical support function for Prefect's customers across the Prefect and Dagster product lines. Its mission is to resolve customer technical issues with the least possible customer effort, and to prevent those issues from recurring.
We are hiring a Developer Success Engineer to work the combined Prefect and Dagster support queue. You will diagnose and resolve technical issues in customer environments, own each issue through resolution, and contribute to the documentation, tooling, and product feedback that reduce future volume. You will be trained on both Prefect’s and Dagster’s products.
The team is investing in agent-based automation for routine support work, which is moving the engineering focus toward complex diagnosis and escalation. This role is well suited to an engineer who wants to build deep expertise in orchestration and data platform environments and apply it directly with customers.
## What You'll Do
* **Clear the failure state, and prevent the next one.** Diagnose problems across Prefect and Dagster installations, integrations, deployments, and the cloud and container environments they run in. Find the underlying "why" so your first response resolves the question and pre-empts the follow-ups. Turn what you learn into docs, debugging resources, and tooling that deflect repeat submissions.
* **Own what's ours; say no clearly to what isn't.** Take full accountability for root causes inside our products' domain of control. For problems outside our Scope of Support, issue a principled no that still gives the customer a way forward. Helplessness erodes trust as fast as a wrong answer.
* **Support your findings, and ask customers to support theirs.** Back every diagnosis with evidence and logic. Assume the customer is the expert on their own stack, ask for what you need to troubleshoot both sides of an issue, and explain why you need it. Leave room for the possibility you've missed something.
* **Give the best possible update every time, and say so when you're still building it.** A half-baked answer sent fast is worse than a complete one sent when it's ready; but radio silence is worse than both. When an issue needs to be escalated, you stay the customer's single point of contact, keep them updated on a regular cadence, and close the loop.
* **Feed the product.** File reproducible product issues and surface recurring failure patterns to Engineering and Product.
You'll work the queue independently on day-to-day issues and own moderate-complexity problems end to end, including investigations across a customer's cloud environment. You'll ask when the Scope of Support or an escalation path is unclear, and you'll build the judgment to recognize when an issue belongs with Customer Engineering or a CSM instead. We measure the role on Customer Effort Score and resolution time, held in tension: a fast answer that costs the customer effort isn't a good one.
**Timezone & on‐call:** Available to work 09:00 – 18:00 CET (UTC ± 2) and participate in the 24/7 on‐call rotations.
## Your Qualifications
**Must have:**
* Python fluency at the level of reading and debugging someone else's code, not only writing your own.
* Hands-on experience running workloads in at least one major cloud and in containers or Kubernetes, enough to troubleshoot a deployment you didn't build.
* Experience with a workflow orchestrator (Prefect, Dagster, Airflow, or comparable) and a strong interest in the data engineering space it lives in.
* A track record of technical, customer-facing work: support, solutions engineering, developer relations, or similar.
* Clear enough written communication to explain a root cause to a skeptical senior engineer and earn their trust.
**Nice to have:**
* Direct experience with Prefect or Dagster specifically.
* A history of open-source contribution, in any project.
* SQL and data warehouse familiarity.
* Experience building support tooling or automation.
## What to expect
This is a support role. There's a queue, a Scope of Support, and an on-call rotation, and the first job is always the failure state in front of you. If a defined scope and a real customer on the other end of every problem sounds like the point, this is the role. # Senior People Systems & Operations Lead - London
People & Talent - London - Onsite - Full Time
Overview
Application Form
### ****Why We Exist****
The world is moving away from rigid ownership models in favour of more flexible, affordable access. Yet the $1.5 trillion device market has barely moved.
Our mission is to transform how technology is bought, used and reused — creating better outcomes for customers, brands and the planet.
### ****What We've Built****
Raylo is the subscription infrastructure that enables leading electronics brands, including PlayStation, HP and Dyson, to move from one-off device sales to recurring subscription programmes that increase conversion, deepen loyalty and capture more lifetime value.
We have over $100m ARR, we’re profitable, growing fast, with over a quarter of a million subscriptions across consumers and small businesses. Customers trust us too, with a 4.5/5 Trustpilot rating from more than 20,000 reviews.
For customers, the experience is simple: subscribe to a device, get support throughout, upgrade when you want, and return it when you’re done. Behind that sits an AI-powered operating system that executes and manages device subscriptions end to end: credit and fraud decisioning, lifecycle operations, and the financing engine that enables brands to run subscription programmes at scale.
Brands can unlock a powerful new growth engine with Raylo across embedded checkout, Raylo.com and the customer app — converting more DTC customers, reaching subscription-first demand, and driving repeat upgrades that compound customer lifetime value.
The impact of our circular model is big. We cut emissions per device by around 50% compared to buy-and-discard. We’re B Corp certified, backed by Macquarie, NatWest and Channel 4 Ventures, and recognised by Tech Nation’s Future Fifty.
### ****How We Work****
AI is changing what small, ambitious teams can build. Companies that embrace it will define the next decade.
Raylo is uniquely placed to benefit. We combine proprietary technology and data with the orchestration of physical assets, operating across credit, fraud, pricing, logistics, refurbishment, resale and customer care. With AI improving every cycle, our moat deepens with scale.
At Raylo, AI is woven into how we work every day. We don’t ration access or hedge our bets. Our people use the best models and tools, and we expect them to do things that weren’t possible a year ago. Processes that used to be good enough are being rebuilt. Teams are replacing spreadsheets with bespoke tooling, and anyone can query our data layer in plain English and get a real answer in seconds.
We give every team their own hackathon: a chance to step back, start with a blank sheet, and ask: if we were starting today, how would we do this?
The more we automate, the more human judgement matters. AI gives people back time, and we expect them to spend it on the things no model can replicate: conversations, trust, craft and team judgement.
We hire to a high bar. You’ll work with people who push you, raise your game and expect you to do the same. We want every person at Raylo to do the best work of their lives, and enjoy doing it.
### ****Our Core Values****
****💡 Be deeply curious**** – We thrive on innovation through diverse approaches, views, and people.
****👟 Walk in your customer’s shoes**** – To build the best products and make the best decisions for the long term, we must figure out what our customers need, not just what they want.
****🎯 Focus and execute**** – We have a big vision, but we believe in nailing the most important problems first.
****💥 Be gritty**** – Only gritty teams succeed. Our individual ownership, passion, and perseverance mean we’re a team through thick and thin.
### ****Your Team****
We're hiring a Senior Systems & Operations Lead to own and scale the operational backbone of our People function, as Raylo grows and expands internationally.
You'll report to our Director of People and be based in our London office, as the first dedicated member of our People Ops team, working closely with the wider People & Talent team across London and Belfast.
AI runs through how we work, and this role builds it in rather than bolting it on. We already use it to draft, automate reporting, and keep systems current. You'll take that further.
### ****What You’ll Do****
* ****Own HR systems and people data**** - keep our systems clean, scalable and structured, so reporting and AI-driven insight are possible.
* ****Own and improve People Ops**** - end-to-end ownership of contracts, employee changes, leavers, onboarding and policy, removing friction as we scale.
* ****Drive compliance and policy**** - own UK employment compliance and lead on US contractor compliance as we expand.
* ****Own L&D infrastructure and workplace experience**** - make sure the tools and sites work, line managing our Office Managers across Belfast and London, while People Partners lead programme design.
* ****Build AI into how People Ops runs**** - design onboarding, policy Q&A, reporting and contract workflows that use AI by default, give managers and employees self-serve tools, and set the guardrails for how we use AI in a people context.
### ****You’ll Succeed With****
* ****AI fluency that goes beyond buzzwords**** - you reach for AI when designing how things should work, not just when told to.
* ****Solid People Ops foundations**** - you know how to run and improve clean, reliable People operations: systems, compliance, contracts, policy, data.
* ****International scaling experience**** - you've built People processes across multiple jurisdictions; US contractor compliance, EOR providers or multi-country onboarding are all relevant.
* ****Systems thinking, and an optimiser's instinct**** - you build things once, properly, and you're as energised by fixing a broken process as by creating something new.
* ****Strong communication**** - you influence senior stakeholders, explain technical concepts simply, and build trust across the business.
### ****Opportunities & Benefits****
🚀 Fast-track your career – 40% of our employees progress every review cycle (bi-annually)
📱 Exclusive Raylo device lease for employees
🏥 Private Medical Insurance
📈 Stock options for all employees
📚 L&D budget to support the skills you value
🏢 Hybrid working model
🌴 33 days off, your way – 25 days + 8 bank holidays with full flexibility to use on the days that mean the most to you
👶 Enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption or shared parental leave, if you've been with us for 12 months.
🧸 Workplace nursery scheme for major cost savings
### ****Hiring Process****
We move quickly and we'll aim to give you the best candidate experience possible. It starts with a 15-minute call — no prep needed. If there's a fit, we move fast, every stage has a purpose, and we'll tell you what we're looking for at each one.
****If there's anything we can do to support you through the process, whether that's adjustments or anything else, please let us know.****
\*As an FCA-regulated business, we conduct background checks (DBS and AML) on all successful candidates who are offered a position at Raylo during the onboarding process. ### ****Diversity & Inclusion at Raylo****
At Raylo, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We welcome people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, believing they make us stronger.

Are you passionate about building AI-enabled products that help editors make better, faster, and more transparent decisions?

About our team
Our team supports the editorial workflows of the largest scientific publisher in the world — millions of manuscript submissions a year, a portfolio of thousands of journals, and tens of thousands of editors. As submission volume grows, we modernise editorial processes, so they scale without compromising the integrity of the scientific record. We are a cross-functional, evidence-led team of engineers, UX, data scientists, product analysts and subject-matter experts, and we work to a simple standard: everything we do is grounded in user needs, and we use evidence to make commercially driven priority decisions.
About the role This role owns a specific, high-value challenge: deep evaluation after peer review — the stage where an editor reads the reviewer reports and decides to accept, reject, or request revision, and ensure the manuscript reaches the publication standard. It is the most time-intensive stage in the workflow and the peak of editorial cognitive load and perceived editorial risk. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager with deep product judgement to own the strategy, vision and roadmap for editorial decision support at the post-peer-review stage. As a product manager for Elsevier’s global Submissions, you will enable growth of knowledge, research and innovation for our researcher community.
You will work within the wider publishing experience. You will help define the path from today’s manual workflow through system-guided support. You will work closely with an embedded data science team to commission and interpret evaluations of decision-support response accuracy, relevance and trust, and partner with the teams that own peer-review analytics and the wider Editor experience pipeline. We’re looking for a Product Manager who stays close to the technology and can reason about how the AI behaves, how it is evaluated, and where the trade-offs lie — while remaining, first and foremost, a product manager rather than an engineer or data scientists.
You will be part of a squad of engineers, UX, subject-matter experts and analysts to create a state-of-the-art user experience for article publication. Strong collaboration with stakeholders in Technology, Operations and Publishing will grow trust & build alignment. Creating solutions that are data-driven will contribute to our innovative culture for our digital submission products and services. You will inspire authors to return to Elsevier for the best experience from submission to trusted publication.

Owning, defining and driving the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for editorial decision-support solutions in the post-peer-review process.
Leading delivery within a cross-functional agile team, managing priorities, maintaining a healthy backlog, and ensuring consistent product delivery.
Partnering with scientific editors to understand decision-making challenges, gather user insights, and translate findings into impactful product improvements.
Championing evidence-based decision-making through qualitative and quantitative research, analytics, experimentation, and clear success metrics.
Collaborating with data science teams to evaluate AI-driven capabilities, including review synthesis, contradiction detection, and evidence linking, and using findings to prioritise enhancements.
Measuring product success through business and user outcomes, defining KPIs and OKRs, communicating value, and assessing build, buy, or partner options.
Working with engineering and technical teams to balance product, technical, and architectural considerations.
Ensuring products support transparency, accountability, and responsible use of AI, with appropriate human oversight and auditability.
Aligning stakeholders across Publishing, Technology, Operations, Editorial Strategy, and Research Integrity to build shared understanding and support.
Supporting go-to-market activities, product launches, customer adoption, and migration planning.

Significant product management experience, including ownership of product strategy, roadmap development, and delivery. Experience with Spec-Driven Development (SDD) is beneficial but not essential.
Strong product judgment and the ability to define complex problems, evaluate trade-offs, and focus on user outcomes.
Demonstrated experience working with AI and machine learning products, including generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), or agent-based workflows.
Strong analytical skills and experience using data, experimentation, and research to inform decisions in uncertain or evolving environments.
Experience leading product initiatives within cross-functional teams and delivering outcomes in complex settings.
Experience collaborating with data scientists and translating model evaluations and insights into product decisions.
An understanding of technical concepts and architectural trade-offs, with the ability to work effectively alongside engineering teams. Experience prototyping with AI tools is helpful but not required.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage technical and non-technical audiences.
Commercial awareness and an understanding of how product decisions contribute to organisational goals and customer value.
Familiarity with scholarly publishing, editorial workflows, peer review, or research integrity is advantageous but not required.

Job Description

Full time
Bristol

Why join Rolls-Royce?
At Rolls-Royce we are proud to be a business that has truly helped to shape the modern world and are committed to always being a force for progress; powering, protecting and connecting people everywhere.
By joining Rolls-Royce, you'll have the opportunity to work on world-class solutions, supported by a culture that believes individuality is our greatest strength, and all perspectives, experiences and backgrounds help us innovate and enable our high-performance culture.
An opportunity has arisen for a Manufacturing Engineer Team Lead – Product Introduction to join the Rolls Royce team in Bristol.
A number of exciting opportunities for Manufacturing Engineering roles are available within our Defence Future Programmes team. These roles present an exciting opportunity to work at the frontline, creating, developing and adapting manufacturing processes that will be introduced and used for years. You would be responsible for ensuring manufacturability of new products and be familiar with “Design for Manufacture”. You will also be required to interact and manage relationships across various different functions internally and externally, ranging from design teams within the IPT, to suppliers and onto directly influencing the customer and their requirements. You will also have experience of Technology Development and Product Introduction methodologies such as Advanced Product Quality Planning and Production Part Approval Process and will be working with internal and external suppliers to create, define and implement several methods of manufacture
Future Programmes UK and International is at the heart of securing the future growth of the Defence business. We are delivering tomorrows technology fast, by bringing together the company’s best engineers, programme managers and business professionals. Working in partnership with Governments, primes and new technology companies across the globe, we deliver future solutions to meet the customers emerging requirements.
The different roles available are within the Future Programmes IPTs and each require differing specific skillsets but have a core “Design for Manufacture” thread. Below is the list of specific skillsets we’re looking for. Please include a covering letter stating your particular experience or area of interest.
Composite material development and/or manufacturing experience
Additive Layer Manufacturing experience of aerospace components
Experience setting up a new factory, designing layouts, specifying machines
Single crystal casting experience
Supplier development / supplier capability assessments
Design for Manufacture / Design for Assembly
Design for manufacture for low-cost applications
Future Programmes is looking for someone with drive, passion and commitment who can:
Embrace agility – you will be able to respond quickly to challenges and be able to manage progress despite, missing, ambiguous, or changing requirements.
Bold – you believe in yourself and the team to bravely push the boundaries, and feel comfortable with ‘failing fast’ to pursue rapid knowledge capture.
Pursue collaboration – you find strength in working with others, both inside and outside of our business, and value the diversity of people and perspectives.
Seeks simplicity – you keep it simple and remove complexity, in how you communicate and the way you work.
What you will be doing
Create, develop, implement, validate, maintain and continuously improve manufacturing processes, digital systems and/or methods of manufacture which are capable of meeting and continue to meet requirements for safety, quality, cost, delivery rate and lead time.
Ensure that new manufacturing processes and materials are in full compliance to Health, Safety & Environmental Standards and meet the expectations of the Zero Harm Programme.
Develop and influence design and manufacturing requirements, through manufacturing trials and working concurrently with a large number of internal and external stakeholders, including the design function, the supply chain and the customer.
Work with an extensive UK supply chain, and subject matter experts to ensure all manufacturing processes are developed in a manner that meets the business needs of Rolls-Royce, (including taking, Safety, Cost, Quality, Delivery and People into consideration) to enable processes to be integrated to a Rolls-Royce site, if required.
Identify and develop opportunities for new or improved manufacturing processes, digital systems & technologies to meet current or future requirements.
Manage and communicate change effectively and regularly, to a wide range of stakeholders, including programme directors, customers and the supply chain.
Manage budgets, resource and technical content to deliver internal capability, in-line with programme requirements, and present progress reports to key stakeholders.
Responsible for self-development to meet the required competencies for the role. Provides coaching and technical support to others within their area of competence.
Who we’re looking for
Professionally Qualified Engineer (e.g. UK minimum HND/Foundation degree or other national equivalent).
Recognised national or international engineering accreditation (e.g. UK IEng or CEng) where available.
Demonstrated experience in manufacturing processes used within Aerospace (or an equivalent regulated industry) and process development methodologies (e.g. Advanced Product Quality Planning).
Experience of other advanced or emerging manufacturing technology preferred but not essential.
General awareness of Manufacturing Systems and enabling software tools used to develop and analyse manufacturing processes (e.g. CAD/CAM, Statistical Process Control).

Work in a safety-first environment were doing the right thing and keeping it simple are core principles.
Join a culture that values making a real difference through your work.
Develop your career as a mid-career professional blending technical expertise with strong personal qualities.
Thrive in a role that encourages integrity, accountability, resilience, and curiosity.
Collaborate and build relationships in a team-focused environment while also working independently.
Take initiative, lead, and make smart decisions with confidence and support.

About us Salience Labs is building an industry-defining approach to optical circuit switching for AI infrastructure, engineered for real latency reduction and cost savings. We're moving towards real-world deployment, and joining at this stage means genuine ownership over that next chapter, working alongside a highly technical team on one of the most consequential problems in AI infrastructure today.
The Role
You will be joining a multi-disciplinary research team in the UK, working closely with other engineers, to lead the development of III-V active components – primarily semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) – integrated on our silicon. As the technical owner of our SOA technology, you will take devices from epitaxial stack and device design, through fabrication with our III-V and silicon photonics foundry partners, to characterisation, reliability and qualification.
What you'll be doing
Work hands-on and lead the design and modelling of III-V SOAs and related active components, including epitaxial layer structure, gain and saturation power modelling, optical mode design, and electrical and thermal design
Own the SOA technology roadmap and device specifications, translating system requirements (gain, saturation output power, noise figure, polarization dependence, linearity and thermal budget) into device design and integration targets
Lead mask design and tape-outs: generate and review GDS layouts, test structures and design-of-experiment splits
Manage fabrication runs with external epitaxy, III-V and silicon photonics foundry partners: define process flows and specifications, review process and in-line data, resolve yield issues and support the transition into volume manufacturing
Define and lead the characterisation strategy for SOAs at wafer, chip and integrated-PIC level (LIV, gain and ASE spectra, noise figure, saturation output power, polarisation-dependent gain, temperature dependence), including building and automating test setups
Analyse test data, correlate measured performance with design and process variations, identify performance gaps and drive design iterations to close them
Work with packaging and reliability engineers on burn-in, accelerated ageing, failure analysis and qualification of SOA devices
Mentor engineers now and, as the team grows, recruit, line-manage and develop a small team of III-V design and test engineers
Essential requirements
Ph.D. in physics, photonics, electrical engineering, optical engineering or a related subject with 6+ years’ relevant experience, or a Master’s degree with 8+ years’ relevant experience; including at least 4 years’ hands-on development of III-V SOAs or semiconductor lasers, preferably in industry
Demonstrated track record of taking SOAs (or semiconductor lasers) from concept through design, fabrication and test, ideally including devices taken through qualification
Deep understanding of semiconductor laser and amplifier physics: optical gain, carrier dynamics, quantum-well design, amplified spontaneous emission and noise, gain saturation and nonlinearities, thermal effects and polarisation dependence
Hands-on knowledge of III-V epitaxy and fabrication processes (e.g. MOCVD/MBE growth, lithography, etching, passivation, metallisation, facet/AR coating), and experience working with external foundries
Experience with characterising SOAs or lasers, including optical spectrum analysers, gain and noise-figure measurement, wafer-level probing, temperature-controlled testing and test automation
Experience with mainstream simulation and layout tools for active and passive photonic devices, such as Lumerical (including MQW/CHARGE/HEAT), Photon Design (PICWave, FIMMWAVE/Harold), Crosslight, RSoft, COMSOL, KLayout, L-Edit or Cadence Virtuoso
Proven ability to lead technical projects and coordinate across design, process, test and packaging functions, together with experience mentoring or supervising engineers
Excellent communication skills, critical thinking, attention to detail and self-motivation
Nice to have
Experience integrating III-V active devices with silicon photonics, including mode conversion and coupling design between III-V and silicon waveguides
Experience line-managing a technical team, including recruitment and performance development
Experience with reliability testing and failure analysis of III-V devices (e.g. accelerated ageing, catastrophic optical damage)
Experience developing PDK building blocks or compact models for active devices
Experience in programming languages, such as Python, MATLAB or C++, for simulation, test automation and data analysis
Knowledge of photonic packaging, including fibre coupling, thermal design and TEC control
Demonstrated ability to generate high quality patents and research papers

We are about to begin rolling out our service with a major French electricity transmission operator. Successfully introducing a new operational capability into an organisation of this scale requires more than delivering the technology.
The customer needs to understand where the value lies, how the service fits into its wider operation and what successful adoption looks like. Different stakeholders will have different priorities, and the scope of the relationship will continue to develop as both organisations learn more.
You will become the senior owner of that relationship, while helping sees.ai develop and manage similar relationships with infrastructure operators across Europe.
Working directly with senior customer stakeholders, you will help define the business case for each phase of these relationships, establish how success will be measured and ensure that customers can see the value sees.ai is creating.
You will work alongside our Client Delivery, Operations, Engineering and Commercial teams to turn those customer objectives into something sees.ai can deliver credibly and commercially.
**Details: -**

## The context
Energy grids worldwide are under enormous pressure from rising demand, ageing infrastructure and the transition to renewable generation. Operators need more frequent, consistent and detailed information about their networks than conventional inspection methods can provide.
sees.ai collects and delivers that information safely and at scale using autonomous UAS.
Today, the data primarily consists of high-resolution imagery, with the capability extending to video, thermal imaging and LiDAR. We develop the entire system in-house: the UAS, ground-control systems, cloud software and field operation itself.
Our work with National Grid in the UK has already progressed from trials into full operational service. France is our first major expansion market beyond the UK and represents the next important stage of our international growth.
This role will help shape and support that rollout, while developing the customer relationships that will underpin sees.ai’s broader expansion across Europe.
## What you will do
* Become sees.ai’s senior relationship owner for key European customers, beginning with a major French electricity transmission operator moving into operational rollout.
* Work with customers to define the business case, outcomes and measures of success for each stage of the relationship.
* Translate emerging customer needs into clear briefs, working with Client Delivery, Operations and Engineering to ensure that sees.ai’s response is credible and deliverable.
* Establish and run formal account governance, including executive steering committees, performance reviews, reporting and senior escalation.
* Lead contract renewal, scope and pricing discussions, working with Commercial, Finance and Legal to agree sustainable terms.
* Identify and develop opportunities to extend sees.ai’s work across customers’ networks and operations.
* Manage the transition of relationships from sees.ai’s existing senior stakeholders, then build and lead the Customer Success team required as our European customer base grows.

* Fluent spoken and written French and English, with the ability to lead executive meetings, workshops and commercial discussions in both languages.
* Significant experience owning and growing complex, high-value enterprise customer relationships.
* Experience working with senior stakeholders inside large, complex or highly regulated organisations.
* A track record of developing a business case or commercial brief collaboratively with a customer.
* The ability to establish where customer value lies and translate it into clear outcomes and measures.
* Experience managing strategic accounts through a significant transition, such as moving from trial or pilot into wider commercial adoption.

* Experience establishing and running formal customer governance, including steering committees and structured reporting.
* The ability to work effectively alongside Delivery, Operations, Product and Engineering without blurring ownership or making commitments on their behalf.
* Confidence managing senior escalations while preserving trust and maintaining clear expectations.
* Experience building and leading teams.
* Willingness to travel regularly to France and elsewhere in Europe.
## Desirable skills and experience
* Experience in energy, utilities, infrastructure, aviation or another safety-critical or regulated industry.
* Experience working with transmission or distribution system operators, national infrastructure organisations or public-sector customers.
* Experience helping customers adopt a new operational technology or service at scale.

* Our customer has a clear and evidenced business case for moving from trial into wider operational use.

* Customer Success and Client Delivery have clearly defined and effective responsibilities.
* Customers receive consistent, accurate governance and can see how delivery performance connects to the value they are seeking.

* New opportunities across Europe are identified, assessed and converted into well-defined areas of work.

job_description:
# Experiential Marketing Lead (Head of Shopify Spaces, London)
* Remote - United Kingdom
* Creative
## About the role
We believe brand is built in the moments people remember, and few moments stick like being in the room. Events are among the hardest things in marketing to attribute and among the easiest to remember. Nobody decides to start a business because of an ad. They decide because they met someone, heard something, tried something, or saw what was possible up close. We want Shopify to be where that happens.
Shopify is coming to London with its first permanent London Space: a hub for the people turning ideas into companies, side hustles into million-pound brands, and local communities into global commerce movements. On the surface, this will be a beautiful room where Shopify hosts founder talks, product education, retail pop-ups, product launches, and cultural moments. The real job is more interesting: make the Space proof that the future of commerce is already happening here.
Our New York Space has shown what happens when commerce and culture are woven together: 100K+ annual visitors, high-signal brand and creator activations, and moments people keep talking about after they leave, from celebrity-founder pop-ups to tent-pole activations around Marathon Weekend and Fashion Week. London deserves its own version, not a copy/paste of what we have already done. It needs someone with the taste and nerve to make it feel unmistakably of the city.
We’re hiring a Head of Spaces, London to build the experiential program strategy for the Space and run the room: programming, production, community, operations, team, partners, and the culture and quality bar. Your work will help entrepreneurs in London become more successful, make Shopify’s role in retail commerce impossible to miss, and turn the Space into a brand channel that travels far beyond the people who were there in person.
If your instinct is to maximize the calendar, this will be a frustrating role. If your instinct is to ask what people will still be talking about in a month, it will not.
# What you’ll do
* **Build the London strategy for Shopify Spaces.** Define the programming thesis, roadmap, budget, KPI model, and operating cadence for a Space whose job is to make Shopify unmistakably useful and culturally relevant for London entrepreneurs, retailers, creators, and commerce communities.
* **Make the case for why Spaces matter.** Turn the London Space into a strategic asset for Shopify: a place where entrepreneurs get more successful, our role in retail and commerce becomes tangible, and the brand earns attention because the work is useful, surprising, and worth sharing.
* **Build the system, not just the calendar.** Establish how ideas are sourced, briefed, greenlit, produced, marketed, measured, and, when they are not strong enough, killed.
* **Act as curator-in-chief.** Be the gatekeeper for only “hell yes” opportunities. Program a mix of pop-ups, founder salons, product education, retail experiments, community dinners, workshops, talks, launches, and cultural moments that feel inevitable, not busy.
* **Make London feel like London.** Stay close to the founders, retailers, creatives, agencies, communities, neighbourhoods, and brands shaping commerce in the city. Spot the people worth backing before they are obvious.
* **Produce moments people repeat.** Own the end-to-end experience with your team, including the tiny details people remember without knowing why. The work should be strong enough in the room and interesting enough to travel on social afterwards.
* **Use the product, not just the logo.** Make Shopify’s commerce platform visible in retail experiments and pop-up infrastructure, from Point of Sale to Shop App moments like geo-gated drops, merchant storytelling, inventory, payments, and checkout.
* **Build the team.** Hire, manage, and develop the soon-to-be-built London Spaces team, including senior event producers, event operations, and partnership marketing roles.
* **Own the partner and vendor ecosystem.** Establish and manage relationships with experiential agencies, freelancers, fabricators, AV teams, caterers, staffing partners, security, and local collaborators who determine whether an idea survives contact with reality.
* **Run the machine.** Own the practical reality of a permanent Space, including budgets, security, storage, AV, maintenance, rituals, and operating standards that keep the Space sharp every day.
* **Measure what actually matters.** Attendance, qualified community growth, pipeline influence, product engagement, partner value, and earned attention all matter. So do the harder-to-measure moments that make people feel inspired, connected, and more likely to build with Shopify.
# What we’re looking for
* **Founder-grade experiential judgement.** You have built events, spaces, festivals, pop-ups, communities, or cultural programs where the stakes were real and the details mattered. You know because you have done it, not because you supervised from a distance.
* **Taste, demonstrably.** A body of work you can point to, defend, and critique honestly.
* **Cultural fluency in London.** You know when to show up and when to sit out. You understand where entrepreneurs, retailers, creators, and communities actually gather, not just where trend reports say they do.
* **Production fluency.** Credibility with the vendors and partners who make the work real. You can speak confidently with fabricators, AV teams, caterers, staffing partners, agencies, security, and landlords.
* **Systems thinking.** You can hold a three-year ambition and a broken microphone in the same afternoon. You build the process that lets creative work scale without sanding off its edge.
* **Senior influence.** You can advise executives and make a case with sharp reasoning rather than consensus theatre.
* **Operational nerve.** You are calm inside complexity and can make order out of chaos.
* **Curious about commerce and technology.** You do not need to be a Shopify expert on day one. You do need to care about entrepreneurs, retail, culture, and the pace of change in commerce.
This role probably is not for you if your strongest work is executing someone else’s event brief inside an established machine. We need someone who can design the operating system for a new Space, set a high creative bar, know which opportunities deserve a hard no, and still break the pattern when the right idea comes along.
# Practical details
* This is a hybrid London-based role. Expect to spend more time on site in year one while building out the strategy, operating rhythm, and team.
* At full operation, expect to work from the London Space approximately three days a week, with flexibility around major activations.
* Some programming will happen at night or on weekends. This is part of the role.
* Occasional travel may be required.
# How to apply
No cover letters. Send a CV or portfolio link if it helps us understand your work. In the application below, we're going to ask these two questions. These questions are about taste, cultural understanding, and how you see London.
1. **Who would make the line go around the block?** Name one relatively unheard-of London-based brand, business, creator, founder, community, or shop you would partner with for the Space. What would you build with them, who would come, and why should Shopify be the one to host it?
2. **Where do London entrepreneurs actually hang out?** We’re new to London. Give us a short map, list, voice note, deck, or memo of the physical places, rooms, shops, studios, communities, and neighbourhoods we should understand before opening. Tell us the five you would visit first and why.
## About Shopify
Opportunity is not evenly distributed. Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to over 8,300 employees and generated over $1 trillion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries.
This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option.
## About you
Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means Shopify is not the right place for everyone.
Before you apply, consider if you can:
* Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone
* Excel by seeking professional and personal hypergrowth
* Keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter)
* Be resilient and resourceful in face of ambiguity and thrive on (rather than endure) change
* Bring critical thought and opinion
* Put AI agents and tools to work on the tasks they're built for, and focus on the work only humans can do
* Embrace differences and disagreement to get shit done and move forward
* Work digital-first for your daily work
*We may use AI-enabled tools to screen, select, and assess applications. All AI outputs are reviewed and validated by our recruitment team.*
